verses.1:1: Now after the death of Joshua, the sons of Israel inquired of the LORD, saying, "Who will go up for us against the Canaanites first to fight them?"
verses.1:2: And the LORD said, "Judah will go up. Look, I have given the land into his hand."
verses.1:3: Then Judah said to his brother Simeon, "Come up with me into my allotment so that we may fight against the Canaanites, and I too will go with you into your allotment." So Simeon went with him.
verses.1:4: Judah went up, and the LORD gave the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand, and they struck them down at Bezek, ten thousand men.
verses.1:5: They found Adoni-bezek at Bezek and fought against him, and they struck down the Canaanites and the Perizzites.
verses.1:6: Adoni-bezek fled, but they pursued after him, seized him, and cut off his thumbs and his big toes.
verses.1:7: Adoni-bezek said, "Seventy kings with their thumbs and big toes cut off used to glean under my table. Just as I have done, so God has repaid me." Then they brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.
verses.1:8: Then the sons of Judah fought against Jerusalem and captured it; they struck it with the edge of the sword and set the city on fire.
verses.1:9: Afterward the sons of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Negev, and the lowland.
verses.1:10: So Judah went against the Canaanites who lived in Hebron—now the name of Hebron formerly was Kiriath-arba—and they struck down Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.
verses.1:11: From there he went against the inhabitants of Debir; now the name of Debir formerly was Kiriath-sepher.
verses.1:12: Caleb said, "Whoever strikes Kiriath-sepher and captures it, to him I will give my daughter Achsah as a wife."
verses.1:13: Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, captured it, so he gave him his daughter Achsah as a wife.
verses.1:14: Now when she arrived, she urged him to ask her father for the field. Then she dismounted from the donkey, and Caleb said to her, "What is it you want?"
verses.1:15: She said to him, "Grant me a blessing, for you have given me the land of the Negev; now give me springs of water too." Then Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.
verses.1:16: Now the sons of the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law, went up from the City of Palms with the sons of Judah to the wilderness of Judah, which is in the Negev of Arad, and they went and lived with the people.
verses.1:17: Then Judah went with his brother Simeon, and they struck down the Canaanites who lived in Zephath and devoted it to destruction; so he called the name of the city Hormah.
verses.1:18: And Judah captured Gaza and its territory, Ashkelon and its territory, and Ekron and its territory.
verses.1:19: The LORD was with Judah, and he took possession of the hill country, yet he could not dispossess the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.
verses.1:20: They gave Hebron to Caleb, just as Moses had spoken, and from there he drove out the three sons of Anak.
verses.1:21: Yet the sons of Benjamin did not dispossess the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem, so the Jebusites have lived with the sons of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.
verses.1:22: Now the house of Joseph also went up to Bethel, and the LORD was with them.
verses.1:23: The house of Joseph had Bethel scouted out; now the name of the city formerly was Luz.
verses.1:24: The lookouts saw a man coming out of the city and said to him, "Please show us the entrance of the city, and we will show kindness to you."
verses.1:25: So he showed them the entrance of the city, and they struck the city with the edge of the sword, but they let the man and all his family go.
verses.1:26: Then the man went into the land of the Hittites, built a city, and called its name Luz; that is its name to this day.
verses.1:27: Manasseh did not dispossess Beth-shean and its daughter towns, nor Taanach and its daughter towns, nor the inhabitants of Dor and its daughter towns, nor the inhabitants of Ibleam and its daughter towns, nor the inhabitants of Megiddo and its daughter towns; so the Canaanites were determined to live in that land.
verses.1:28: When Israel grew strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, yet they did not completely dispossess them.
verses.1:29: And Ephraim did not dispossess the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived in their midst in Gezer.
verses.1:30: Zebulun did not dispossess the inhabitants of Kitron or the inhabitants of Nahalol, so the Canaanites lived in their midst and became subject to forced labor.
verses.1:31: Asher did not dispossess the inhabitants of Acco or the inhabitants of Sidon, nor Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, or Rehob.
verses.1:32: So the Asherites lived in the midst of the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, for they did not dispossess them.
verses.1:33: Naphtali did not dispossess the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh or the inhabitants of Beth-anath, but lived in the midst of the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land; yet the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath became subject to forced labor for them.
verses.1:34: Then the Amorites pressed the sons of Dan back into the hill country, for they did not allow them to go down into the valley.
verses.1:35: The Amorites were determined to live in Mount Heres, in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim, yet the hand of the house of Joseph grew heavy, and they became subject to forced labor.
verses.1:36: Now the border of the Amorites was from the ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela and upward.
verses.2:1: The angel of the LORD went up from Gilgal to Bochim and said, "I brought you up from Egypt and brought you to the land that I swore to your fathers, and I said, 'I will never break My covenant with you,
verses.2:2: and as for you, you must not make a covenant with the inhabitants of this land; you must tear down their altars.' Yet you have not obeyed My voice. What is this that you have done?
verses.2:3: So I also said, 'I will not drive them out from before you; they will become thorns in your sides, and their gods will become a snare to you.'"
verses.2:4: Now when the angel of the LORD spoke these words to all the sons of Israel, the people raised their voices and wept.
verses.2:5: So they called the name of that place Bochim, and they sacrificed there to the LORD.
verses.2:6: Now Joshua sent the people away, and the sons of Israel went, each to his inheritance, to possess the land.
verses.2:7: The people served the LORD all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who lived on after Joshua, who had seen all the great work of the LORD that He had done for Israel.
verses.2:8: Then Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at one hundred and ten years of age.
verses.2:9: They buried him within the territory of his inheritance, in Timnath-heres, in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
verses.2:10: All of that generation were likewise gathered to their fathers, and another generation arose after them who did not know the LORD, nor even the work that He had done for Israel.
verses.2:11: Then the sons of Israel did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD and served the Baals.
verses.2:12: They abandoned the LORD, the God of their fathers, who had brought them out of the land of Egypt, and they went after other gods from among the gods of the peoples around them and bowed down to them, and they provoked the LORD to anger.
verses.2:13: So they abandoned the LORD and served Baal and the Ashtaroth.
verses.2:14: Then the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He gave them into the hand of plunderers, and they plundered them; He also sold them into the hand of their enemies on every side, so that they were no longer able to stand before their enemies.
verses.2:15: Wherever they went out, the hand of the LORD was against them for harm, just as the LORD had spoken and just as the LORD had sworn to them; and they were in extreme distress.
verses.2:16: Then the LORD raised up judges, and they delivered them from the hand of their plunderers.
verses.2:17: Yet they did not listen even to their judges, for they prostituted themselves after other gods and bowed down to them. They turned aside quickly from the way in which their fathers had walked in obeying the commandments of the LORD; they did not do so.
verses.2:18: Whenever the LORD raised up judges for them, the LORD was with the judge and delivered them from the hand of their enemies all the days of the judge; for the LORD was moved to pity by their groaning because of those who oppressed and afflicted them.
verses.2:19: Yet whenever the judge died, they would turn back and act more corruptly than their fathers, going after other gods to serve them and to bow down to them. They did not give up any of their practices or their stubborn way.
verses.2:20: So the anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and He said, "Because this nation has transgressed My covenant that I commanded their fathers and has not obeyed My voice,
verses.2:21: I too will no longer drive out anyone from before them of the nations that Joshua left when he died,
verses.2:22: in order to test Israel by them, whether they will keep the way of the LORD to walk in it just as their fathers kept it, or not."
verses.2:23: So the LORD left those nations, without driving them out quickly, and He did not give them into the hand of Joshua.
verses.3:1: These are the nations that the LORD left behind to test Israel through them, all those who had not known any of the wars of Canaan,
verses.3:2: only so that the generations of the sons of Israel might know, to instruct them in war—at least those who previously had not known them:
verses.3:3: the five rulers of the Philistines, and all the Canaanites, and the Sidonians, and the Hivites who inhabited Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal-hermon as far as Lebo-hamath.
verses.3:4: They were there to test Israel through them, to know whether they would obey the commands of the LORD that He had commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.
verses.3:5: And the sons of Israel lived in the midst of the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
verses.3:6: They took their daughters as wives for themselves, their own daughters they gave to their sons, and they served their gods.
verses.3:7: So the sons of Israel did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD; they forgot the LORD their God, and they served the Baals and the Asherahs.
verses.3:8: Then the LORD's anger burned against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram-naharaim; and the sons of Israel served Cushan-rishathaim for eight years.
verses.3:9: Then the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for the sons of Israel, and he delivered them: Othniel son of Kenaz, the younger brother of Caleb.
verses.3:10: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him, and he judged Israel. He went out to war, and the LORD gave Cushan-rishathaim king of Aram into his hand, and his hand prevailed over Cushan-rishathaim.
verses.3:11: So the land was quiet for forty years, and Othniel son of Kenaz died.
verses.3:12: Then the sons of Israel again did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, so the LORD strengthened Eglon king of Moab against Israel because they had done what was evil in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.3:13: He gathered the sons of Ammon and Amalek to himself, went and struck Israel, and they took possession of the City of Palms.
verses.3:14: So the sons of Israel served Eglon king of Moab for eighteen years.
verses.3:15: Then the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD, and the LORD raised up a deliverer for them: Ehud son of Gera, the Benjaminite, a left-handed man. And the sons of Israel sent tribute by his hand to Eglon king of Moab.
verses.3:16: Ehud made for himself a sword having two edges, a short cubit long, and he strapped it beneath his garments on his right thigh.
verses.3:17: He presented the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon was a very fat man.
verses.3:18: When he finished presenting the tribute, he dismissed the people who had carried the tribute.
verses.3:19: But he himself turned back from the carved images near Gilgal and said, "I have a secret word for you, King." He said, "Silence!" And all those standing in attendance on him went out from him.
verses.3:20: Then Ehud came to him as he was sitting in the cool upper chamber that was his alone. And Ehud said, "I have a word from God for you." So he rose from the seat.
verses.3:21: Then Ehud extended his left hand, took the sword from his right thigh, and drove it into his belly.
verses.3:22: Even the hilt went in after the blade, and the fat closed over the blade, for he did not pull the sword out of his belly; and the excrement came out.
verses.3:23: Then Ehud went out into the vestibule, shut the doors of the upper chamber behind him, and locked them.
verses.3:24: After he had gone out, his servants came and looked, and see, the doors of the upper chamber were locked. So they said, "Surely he is only relieving himself in the inner room of the cool chamber."
verses.3:25: They waited to the point of embarrassment, and look, he was not opening the doors of the upper chamber. So they took the key and opened them, and there was their master, fallen on the ground, dead.
verses.3:26: Meanwhile, Ehud had escaped while they lingered; he passed beyond the carved images and escaped to Seirah.
verses.3:27: When he arrived, he blew the ram's horn in the hill country of Ephraim; and the sons of Israel went down with him from the hill country, and he was in front of them.
verses.3:28: He said to them, "Pursue after me, for the LORD has given your enemies, Moab, into your hand." So they went down after him and captured the fords of the Jordan toward Moab, and they did not allow anyone to cross over.
verses.3:29: They struck down Moab at that time, about ten thousand men, every one stout and every one a man of valor, and not a man escaped.
verses.3:30: So Moab was subdued on that day under the hand of Israel, and the land was quiet for eighty years.
verses.3:31: After him came Shamgar son of Anath, and he struck down six hundred men of the Philistines with an oxgoad; and he also delivered Israel.
verses.4:1: Then the sons of Israel again did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, after Ehud had died.
verses.4:2: So the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor; the commander of his army was Sisera, and he lived in Harosheth-hagoyim.
verses.4:3: Then the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD, for he had nine hundred chariots of iron, and he oppressed the sons of Israel severely for twenty years.
verses.4:4: And Deborah, a prophetess, wife of Lappidoth, was the one judging Israel at that time.
verses.4:5: She would sit beneath the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the sons of Israel went up to her for judgment.
verses.4:6: She sent and summoned Barak son of Abinoam from Kedesh-naphtali, and said to him, "Has not the LORD, the God of Israel, commanded, 'Go and deploy on Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men from the sons of Naphtali and from the sons of Zebulun,
verses.4:7: and I will draw out to you, to the Wadi Kishon, Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army, and his chariots and his multitude, and I will give him into your hand'?"
verses.4:8: Barak said to her, "If you go with me, then I will go; and if you do not go with me, I will not go."
verses.4:9: She said, "I will certainly go with you; however, the glory will not be yours on the way that you are going, for the LORD will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman." So Deborah rose and went with Barak to Kedesh.
verses.4:10: And Barak mustered Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh; ten thousand men went up following at his feet, and Deborah went up with him.
verses.4:11: Meanwhile, Heber the Kenite had separated from Kain, from the sons of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law, and pitched his tent as far as the oak in Zaanannim, which is beside Kedesh.
verses.4:12: They reported to Sisera that Barak son of Abinoam had gone up to Mount Tabor.
verses.4:13: So Sisera mustered all his chariots—nine hundred chariots of iron—and all the people who were with him, from Harosheth-hagoyim to the Wadi Kishon.
verses.4:14: Then Deborah said to Barak, "Rise up, for this is the day that the LORD has given Sisera into your hand! Has not the LORD gone out before you?" So Barak went down from Mount Tabor, with ten thousand men behind him.
verses.4:15: Then the LORD threw Sisera, all the chariots, and the whole army into panic before Barak at the edge of the sword; and Sisera climbed down from the chariot and fled on foot.
verses.4:16: Meanwhile, Barak pursued the chariots and the army as far as Harosheth-hagoyim, and Sisera's entire army fell by the edge of the sword; not even one remained.
verses.4:17: Sisera, however, had fled on foot to the tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite, because there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the household of Heber the Kenite.
verses.4:18: Jael went out to meet Sisera and said to him, "Turn aside, my lord, turn aside to me; do not be afraid." So he turned aside to her into the tent, and she covered him with a blanket.
verses.4:19: He said to her, "Please give me a little water to drink, for I am thirsty." So she opened a skin of milk, gave him a drink, and covered him.
verses.4:20: He said to her, "Stand at the entrance of the tent, and if anyone comes and questions you, saying, 'Is there any man here?' then say, 'No.'"
verses.4:21: Then Jael, the wife of Heber, took a tent peg and placed a hammer in her hand; she came to him stealthily and drove the peg into his temple, and it went down into the ground, for he was in a deep sleep and exhausted; and he died.
verses.4:22: And look, Barak was pursuing Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him and said to him, "Come, let me show you the man you are seeking." So he came in to her, and there was Sisera, fallen dead, with the peg in his temple.
verses.4:23: Thus God subdued Jabin king of Canaan on that day before the sons of Israel.
verses.4:24: And the hand of the sons of Israel bore down harder and harder upon Jabin king of Canaan, until they had cut off Jabin king of Canaan.
verses.5:1: Then Deborah and Barak son of Abinoam sang on that day, saying:
verses.5:2: "When locks hung loose in Israel, when the people offered themselves freely, bless the LORD!
verses.5:3: Listen, kings; give ear, rulers! I, yes I, will sing to the LORD; I will make music to the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.5:4: LORD, when You came out from Seir, when You strode from the country of Edom, the earth shook, the skies too dripped, the clouds too dripped water.
verses.5:5: The mountains streamed before the LORD, the One of Sinai, before the LORD, the God of Israel.
verses.5:6: In the days of Shamgar son of Anath, in the days of Jael, the roads stood deserted, and those who traveled the paths walked along winding roads.
verses.5:7: The village dwellers ceased in Israel, they ceased, until I arose, Deborah, until I arose, a mother in Israel.
verses.5:8: New gods were chosen; then fighting was at the gates. Was a shield seen, or a spear, among forty thousand in Israel?
verses.5:9: My heart is with the commanders of Israel, those who offered themselves freely among the people. Bless the LORD!
verses.5:10: You who ride white donkeys, who sit on carpets, and who walk along the road, recount it!
verses.5:11: Away from the sound of archers among the watering troughs, there they recount the righteous deeds of the LORD, the righteous deeds of His village dwellers in Israel. Then the people of the LORD went down to the gates.
verses.5:12: Wake up, wake up, Deborah! Wake up, wake up, utter a song! Rise, Barak, and take captive your captives, son of Abinoam!
verses.5:13: Then a remnant went down to the nobles, the people; the LORD went down for me among the mighty warriors.
verses.5:14: From Ephraim came those whose root is in Amalek; after you, Benjamin, among your peoples; from Machir commanders went down, and from Zebulun those who wield the scribe's staff.
verses.5:15: And my princes in Issachar were with Deborah, and Issachar was likewise with Barak; into the valley they were sent forth at his heels. Among the divisions of Reuben, great were the resolutions of heart.
verses.5:16: Why did you sit among the sheepfolds, to hear the whistling for the flocks? For the divisions of Reuben, great were the searchings of heart.
verses.5:17: Gilead remained across the Jordan; and Dan, why did he linger by the ships? Asher sat at the coast of the seas and remained by his inlets.
verses.5:18: Zebulun is a people that scorned its life to the point of death, and Naphtali, on the heights of the field.
verses.5:19: Kings came, they fought; then the kings of Canaan fought at Taanach, beside the waters of Megiddo; no gain of silver did they take.
verses.5:20: From the heavens they fought; the stars from their courses fought against Sisera.
verses.5:21: The Kishon torrent swept them away, the ancient torrent, the Kishon torrent. Tread on, my soul, in strength!
verses.5:22: Then the horses' hooves pounded from the galloping, the galloping of his stallions.
verses.5:23: 'Curse Meroz,' said the angel of the LORD, 'curse its inhabitants bitterly, for they did not come to the aid of the LORD, to the aid of the LORD among the mighty warriors.'
verses.5:24: Blessed above women be Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite; above women in the tent may she be blessed.
verses.5:25: Water he asked for, milk she gave; in a nobles' bowl she presented curds.
verses.5:26: She put her hand to the tent peg and her right hand to the laborers' hammer; she hammered Sisera, smashed his head, and shattered and pierced through his temple.
verses.5:27: Between her feet he collapsed, he fell, he lay; between her feet he collapsed, he fell; where he collapsed, there he fell, destroyed.
verses.5:28: Through the window Sisera's mother looked out and wailed through the lattice, 'Why is his chariot so slow to come? Why do the treads of his chariots lag behind?'
verses.5:29: The wisest of her noblewomen answer her; indeed, she repeats her own words to herself:
verses.5:30: 'Are they not finding, dividing plunder—a womb, two wombs for each warrior; plunder of dyed cloths for Sisera, plunder of dyed cloths, embroidery, a dyed cloth of double embroidery for the necks of the plunder?'
verses.5:31: So may all Your enemies perish, LORD, but may those who love Him be like the sun coming out in its strength." And the land was quiet for forty years.
verses.6:1: Then the sons of Israel did evil in the eyes of the LORD, so the LORD gave them into the hand of Midian for seven years.
verses.6:2: The hand of Midian grew strong over Israel; because of Midian, the sons of Israel made for themselves the clefts that are in the mountains, along with the caves and the strongholds.
verses.6:3: Whenever Israel sowed, Midian and Amalek and the sons of the east would come up; yes, they would come up against them.
verses.6:4: They would encamp against them and devastate the produce of the land as far as the approach to Gaza, leaving no sustenance in Israel, nor sheep, nor ox, nor donkey.
verses.6:5: For they and their livestock would come up, along with their tents, and they would come in like locusts in multitude; both they and their camels were without number, and they came into the land to devastate it.
verses.6:6: Thus Israel was greatly impoverished because of Midian, and the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD.
verses.6:7: Now when the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD on account of Midian,
verses.6:8: the LORD sent a prophet to the sons of Israel, and he said to them, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: I Myself brought you up from Egypt and led you out of the house of slaves.
verses.6:9: I rescued you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all your oppressors, and I drove them out from before you and gave their land to you.
verses.6:10: And I told you, 'I am the LORD your God; do not fear the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you live.' Yet you have not listened to My voice."
verses.6:11: Then the angel of the LORD came and sat beneath the terebinth in Ophrah that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite, while Gideon his son was beating out wheat in the winepress to hide it from Midian.
verses.6:12: The angel of the LORD appeared to him and said to him, "The LORD is with you, mighty warrior."
verses.6:13: Gideon said to him, "Pardon me, my lord, if the LORD is with us, why has all this overtaken us? And where are all His wonderful deeds that our fathers recounted to us, saying, 'Did not the LORD bring us up out of Egypt?' Yet now the LORD has deserted us and given us into the grasp of Midian."
verses.6:14: The LORD turned toward him and said, "Go in this strength of yours and save Israel from the grasp of Midian. Have I not sent you?"
verses.6:15: And he said to Him, "Pardon me, Lord, by what means can I save Israel? See, my clan is the poorest in Manasseh, and I am the youngest in my father's house."
verses.6:16: Then the LORD said to him, "Surely I will be with you, and you will strike down Midian as a single man."
verses.6:17: He said to Him, "Please, if I have found favor in Your eyes, perform for me a sign that it is You speaking with me.
verses.6:18: Please do not leave here until I come to You and bring out my offering and place it before You." And He said, "I will stay until you come back."
verses.6:19: Gideon went inside and made ready a young goat and unleavened cakes from an ephah of flour. He put the meat in a basket and put the broth in a pot, and he brought them out to Him beneath the terebinth and presented them.
verses.6:20: The angel of God said to him, "Take the meat and the unleavened cakes, place them on this rock, and pour out the broth." And he did so.
verses.6:21: Then the angel of the LORD stretched out the end of the staff that was in his hand and touched the meat and the unleavened cakes; and fire rose up from the rock and consumed the meat and the unleavened cakes. And the angel of the LORD was gone from his sight.
verses.6:22: Then Gideon saw that he was the angel of the LORD, and Gideon said, "Alas, Lord GOD! For indeed I have seen the angel of the LORD face to face!"
verses.6:23: And the LORD said to him, "Peace to you! Do not be afraid; you will not die."
verses.6:24: So Gideon built an altar there to the LORD and called it The LORD Is Peace. To this day it remains in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
verses.6:25: That night the LORD said to him, "Take the young bull belonging to your father, and the second bull, seven years old, and tear down the altar of Baal that belongs to your father, and cut down the Asherah that is beside it.
verses.6:26: Then build an altar to the LORD your God on top of this stronghold in proper order, and take the second bull and offer a burnt offering with the wood of the Asherah that you cut down."
verses.6:27: So Gideon took ten men from among his servants and did just as the LORD had spoken to him. Because he feared his father's house and the men of the city too much to do it in the daytime, he did it at night.
verses.6:28: When the men of the city got up early in the morning, look—the altar of Baal had been demolished, the Asherah beside it had been cut down, and the second bull had been offered up on the altar that had been built.
verses.6:29: They said to one another, "Who has done this thing?" After inquiring and searching, they said, "Gideon son of Joash has done this thing."
verses.6:30: Then the men of the city said to Joash, "Bring out your son so that he may die, because he has demolished the altar of Baal and because he has cut down the Asherah that was beside it."
verses.6:31: Then Joash said to all who were standing against him, "Are you the ones to contend for Baal, or are you the ones to save him? Whoever contends for him must be put to death by morning. If he is a god, let him contend for himself, because his altar has been demolished."
verses.6:32: So on that day he named him Jerubbaal, saying, "Let Baal contend against him, because he demolished his altar."
verses.6:33: Now all Midian and Amalek and the sons of the east gathered together; they crossed over and encamped in the Valley of Jezreel.
verses.6:34: Then the Spirit of the LORD clothed Gideon; he blew the ram's horn, and Abiezer was summoned to follow him.
verses.6:35: He sent messengers throughout all Manasseh, and they too were summoned to follow him; and he sent messengers into Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they came up to meet them.
verses.6:36: Then Gideon said to God, "If You are indeed going to save Israel by my hand, as You have spoken,
verses.6:37: see, I am setting a wool fleece on the threshing floor. If there is dew on the fleece alone, while all the ground is dry, then I will know that You will save Israel by my hand, as You have spoken."
verses.6:38: And so it was. He got up early the next morning, squeezed the fleece, and wrung dew from the fleece—a bowl full of water.
verses.6:39: Then Gideon said to God, "May Your anger not burn against me while I speak just this once. Please let me test just this one time with the fleece: may it be dry on the fleece alone, while on all the ground there is dew."
verses.6:40: God did so on that night: it was dry on the fleece alone, while on all the ground there was dew.
verses.7:1: Then Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, and all the people who were with him rose early and camped beside the spring of Harod. The camp of Midian was north of him, near the hill of Moreh in the valley.
verses.7:2: The LORD said to Gideon, "The people who are with you are too numerous for Me to give Midian into their hand, otherwise Israel might boast against Me, saying, 'My hand has delivered me.'
verses.7:3: Now therefore, proclaim in the ears of the people, saying, 'Whoever is afraid and trembling, let him turn back and depart from Mount Gilead.'" So twenty-two thousand of the people turned back, and ten thousand remained.
verses.7:4: Then the LORD said to Gideon, "The people are still too numerous. Lead them down to the water, and I will test them for you there. It will be that the one about whom I say to you, 'This one will go with you,' he will go with you; and everyone about whom I say to you, 'This one will not go with you,' he will not go."
verses.7:5: So he led the people down to the water. And the LORD said to Gideon, "Everyone who laps from the water with his tongue as a dog laps, you will set him apart by himself, and likewise everyone who kneels on his knees to drink."
verses.7:6: The number of those who lapped with their hand to their mouth was three hundred men, while all the rest of the people knelt on their knees to drink water.
verses.7:7: The LORD said to Gideon, "With the three hundred men who lapped I will deliver you, and I will give Midian into your hand. Let all the people go, each man to his place."
verses.7:8: So they took the provisions of the people in their hand and their trumpets; and he sent all the men of Israel away, each man to his tents, but he retained the three hundred men. Now the camp of Midian was below him in the valley.
verses.7:9: Now on that night the LORD said to him, "Arise, go down against the camp, for I have given it into your hand.
verses.7:10: But if you are afraid to go down, go down, you and Purah your attendant, to the camp,
verses.7:11: and you will hear what they say; afterward your hands will be strengthened, and you will go down against the camp." So he went down, he and Purah his attendant, to the edge of the armed men who were in the camp.
verses.7:12: Now Midian, Amalek, and all the sons of the east were spread out in the valley like locusts in abundance, and their camels were beyond number, like the sand on the shore of the sea in abundance.
verses.7:13: When Gideon arrived, there was a man recounting a dream to his companion. And he said, "Look, I dreamed a dream, and see, a loaf of barley bread was tumbling into the camp of Midian. It came up to the tent and struck it so that it fell, and it turned it upside down, and the tent lay fallen."
verses.7:14: His companion answered and said, "This is nothing other than the sword of Gideon son of Joash, a man of Israel! God has given Midian and all the camp into his hand."
verses.7:15: When Gideon heard the account of the dream and its interpretation, he bowed down in worship. Then he returned to the camp of Israel and said, "Arise, for the LORD has given the camp of Midian into your hand."
verses.7:16: He divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put trumpets into the hand of every one of them, along with empty jars, and torches inside the jars.
verses.7:17: He said to them, "Watch me and do the same. Now look, I am coming to the edge of the camp, and just as I do, so you will do.
verses.7:18: When I blow the trumpet, I and all who are with me, then you also are to blow the trumpets all around the entire camp and say, 'For the LORD and for Gideon!'"
verses.7:19: So Gideon and the hundred men who were with him came to the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle watch, just after they had posted the watchmen; and they blew the trumpets and smashed the jars that were in their hands.
verses.7:20: Then the three companies blew the trumpets and broke the jars. They grasped the torches in their left hands and the trumpets to blow in their right hands, and they shouted, "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!"
verses.7:21: Each man stood in his place around the camp, while the whole camp ran, cried out, and fled.
verses.7:22: When they blew the three hundred trumpets, the LORD set each man's sword against his companion and throughout the entire camp; and the camp fled as far as Beth-shittah toward Zererah, as far as the border of Abel-meholah, by Tabbath.
verses.7:23: Then the men of Israel were called out from Naphtali, from Asher, and from all Manasseh, and they pursued Midian.
verses.7:24: Gideon also sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Ephraim, saying, "Come down to meet Midian and capture the waters ahead of them as far as Beth-barah, as well as the Jordan." So all the men of Ephraim were called out, and they captured the waters as far as Beth-barah, as well as the Jordan.
verses.7:25: They captured the two commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; they killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and they killed Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb. Then they pursued Midian, and they brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon across the Jordan.
verses.8:1: Then the men of Ephraim said to him, "What is this thing you have done to us, not calling us when you went to fight against Midian?" And they contended fiercely with him.
verses.8:2: He said to them, "What have I done now compared to you? Are not the gleanings of Ephraim better than the grape harvest of Abiezer?
verses.8:3: Into your hand God has given the commanders of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb; and what was I able to do compared to you?" Then their anger against him subsided as he spoke this word.
verses.8:4: Then Gideon reached the Jordan, crossing it, he and the three hundred men who were with him, weary, yet still pursuing.
verses.8:5: He said to the men of Succoth, "Please give loaves of bread to the people who are following me, for they are weary, and I am pursuing Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian."
verses.8:6: The officials of Succoth said, "Are the palms of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand, that we should give bread to your troops?"
verses.8:7: Gideon said, "Therefore, when the LORD gives Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, I will thresh your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with the briers."
verses.8:8: From there he went up to Penuel and spoke to them in the same way; and the men of Penuel answered him just as the men of Succoth had answered.
verses.8:9: So he also said to the men of Penuel, "When I return in peace, I will demolish this tower."
verses.8:10: Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor, and their armies were with them, about fifteen thousand, all who were left from the entire army of the sons of the east; for those who had fallen were one hundred and twenty thousand men who drew the sword.
verses.8:11: Gideon went up by the way of those who dwell in tents, east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and struck the camp while the camp felt secure.
verses.8:12: Zebah and Zalmunna fled, but he pursued them and captured the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and threw the entire camp into panic.
verses.8:13: Then Gideon son of Joash returned from the battle by the ascent of Heres.
verses.8:14: He captured a young man from the men of Succoth and questioned him, and he wrote down for him the officials of Succoth and its elders, seventy-seven men.
verses.8:15: Then he came to the men of Succoth and said, "Here are Zebah and Zalmunna, about whom you taunted me, saying, 'Are the palms of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand, that we should give bread to your weary men?'"
verses.8:16: He took the elders of the city, together with the thorns of the wilderness and the briers, and taught the men of Succoth a lesson with them.
verses.8:17: He also demolished the tower of Penuel and killed the men of the city.
verses.8:18: Then he said to Zebah and Zalmunna, "What were the men like whom you killed at Tabor?" And they said, "As you are, so were they; each one had the appearance of the sons of a king."
verses.8:19: He said, "They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As the LORD lives, if you had kept them alive, I would not kill you."
verses.8:20: He told Jether his firstborn, "Rise up and kill them!" Yet the boy did not draw his sword, for he was afraid, since he was still a boy.
verses.8:21: Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, "Arise yourself and strike us down, for as a man is, so is his might." So Gideon arose and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and he took the crescent ornaments that were on the necks of their camels.
verses.8:22: Then the men of Israel said to Gideon, "Rule over us, you and your son and your son's son as well, for you have delivered us from the hand of Midian."
verses.8:23: Gideon replied to them, "I myself will not rule over you, nor will my son rule over you; the LORD will rule over you."
verses.8:24: Then Gideon said to them, "Let me ask a request of you: let each man give me an earring from his plunder." For they had gold earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.
verses.8:25: They replied, "We will surely give them." So they spread out a cloak, and each man threw an earring from his plunder onto it.
verses.8:26: The weight of the gold earrings that he had requested was one thousand seven hundred shekels of gold, apart from the crescent ornaments, the pendants, and the purple garments that were on the kings of Midian, and apart from the necklaces that were on the necks of their camels.
verses.8:27: Gideon made it into an ephod and set it up in his city, in Ophrah; and all Israel prostituted themselves after it there, so that it became a snare to Gideon and to his household.
verses.8:28: Thus Midian was subdued before the sons of Israel, and they never lifted up their heads again; and the land remained quiet for forty years during the days of Gideon.
verses.8:29: So Jerubbaal son of Joash went away and lived in his house.
verses.8:30: Now Gideon had seventy sons who came from his own loins, because he had many wives.
verses.8:31: His concubine who was in Shechem also bore him a son, and he gave him the name Abimelech.
verses.8:32: Then Gideon son of Joash died at a good old age, and he was buried in the tomb of his father Joash, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
verses.8:33: As soon as Gideon died, the sons of Israel turned back and prostituted themselves after the Baals, and made Baal-berith their god.
verses.8:34: The sons of Israel did not remember the LORD their God, who had rescued them from the hand of all their enemies on every side;
verses.8:35: nor did they show loyal kindness to the household of Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, in accordance with all the good that he had done for Israel.
verses.9:1: Now Abimelech son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem to his mother's brothers, and he spoke to them and to the entire clan of the house of his mother's father, saying,
verses.9:2: "Please speak in the ears of all the lords of Shechem: 'Which is better for you, that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or that one man rule over you?' And remember that I am your bone and your flesh."
verses.9:3: So his mother's brothers spoke all these words on his behalf in the ears of all the lords of Shechem, and their heart turned after Abimelech, for they said, "He is our brother."
verses.9:4: And they gave him seventy silver pieces from the house of Baal-berith, and with them Abimelech hired worthless and reckless men, and they went after him.
verses.9:5: He came to his father's house at Ophrah and killed his brothers, the sons of Jerubbaal, seventy men, on one stone. Yet Jotham, the youngest son of Jerubbaal, remained, because he had hidden himself.
verses.9:6: Then all the lords of Shechem and all of Beth-millo gathered together, and they went and made Abimelech king beside the oak of the pillar that was in Shechem.
verses.9:7: When they told Jotham, he went and stood on the top of Mount Gerizim, lifted up his voice, and called out. And he said to them, "Listen to me, lords of Shechem, so that God may listen to you!
verses.9:8: Indeed, the trees went to anoint a king over themselves, and they said to the olive tree, 'Reign over us.'
verses.9:9: But the olive tree said to them, 'Should I give up my rich oil, since through me they honor God and men, and go to sway over the trees?'
verses.9:10: Then the trees said to the fig tree, 'Come, you reign over us.'
verses.9:11: But the fig tree said to them, 'Should I give up my sweetness and my good produce, and go to sway over the trees?'
verses.9:12: Then the trees said to the vine, 'Come, you reign over us.'
verses.9:13: But the vine said to them, 'Should I give up my new wine, which gladdens God and men, and go to sway over the trees?'
verses.9:14: Then all the trees said to the thornbush, 'Come, you reign over us.'
verses.9:15: And the thornbush said to the trees, 'If in truth you are anointing me to be king over you, come, take shelter in my shade; but if not, let fire come out from the thornbush and devour the cedars of Lebanon.'
verses.9:16: Now then, if you have acted in truth and integrity in making Abimelech king, and if you have done good to Jerubbaal and to his house, and if you have dealt with him according to what his hands deserved—
verses.9:17: for my father fought for you, risked his life, and delivered you from the hand of Midian,
verses.9:18: yet you have risen up against my father's house today, killed his sons, seventy men, on one stone, and made Abimelech, the son of his female servant, king over the lords of Shechem because he is your brother—
verses.9:19: if indeed you have acted in truth and integrity with Jerubbaal and with his house this day, then rejoice in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice in you.
verses.9:20: But if not, let fire come out from Abimelech and devour the lords of Shechem and Beth-millo, and let fire come out from the lords of Shechem and from Beth-millo and devour Abimelech."
verses.9:21: Then Jotham fled and escaped, and went to Beer, and lived there because of Abimelech his brother.
verses.9:22: And Abimelech ruled over Israel for three years.
verses.9:23: Then God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the lords of Shechem, and the lords of Shechem acted treacherously against Abimelech,
verses.9:24: so that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come, and their blood be laid upon Abimelech their brother, who killed them, and upon the lords of Shechem, who strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.
verses.9:25: And the lords of Shechem set ambushers against him on the tops of the mountains, and they robbed everyone who passed by them along the road; and it was reported to Abimelech.
verses.9:26: Now Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers came and crossed over into Shechem, and the lords of Shechem put their trust in him.
verses.9:27: They went out into the field, harvested their vineyards, trod the grapes, and held a festival of praise. Then they entered the house of their god, ate and drank, and cursed Abimelech.
verses.9:28: Then Gaal son of Ebed said, "Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Is he not the son of Jerubbaal, and is not Zebul his officer? Serve the men of Hamor, the father of Shechem! Yet why should we serve him?
verses.9:29: If only this people were given into my hand! Then I would remove Abimelech." And he said to Abimelech, "Enlarge your army and come out!"
verses.9:30: When Zebul, the ruler of the city, heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, his anger burned.
verses.9:31: So he sent messengers to Abimelech secretly, saying, "Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem, and look, they are fortifying the city against you.
verses.9:32: Now therefore, arise by night, you and the people who are with you, and lie in ambush in the field.
verses.9:33: And in the morning, as the sun rises, get up early and rush against the city; and look, when he and the people who are with him come out toward you, you shall do to him whatever your hand finds to do."
verses.9:34: So Abimelech and all the people who were with him arose by night, and they lay in ambush against Shechem in four divisions.
verses.9:35: Then Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at the entrance of the city gate, and Abimelech and the people who were with him arose from the ambush.
verses.9:36: When Gaal saw the people, he said to Zebul, "Look, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains." And Zebul said to him, "It is the shadow of the mountains that you are seeing as men."
verses.9:37: And Gaal spoke yet again and said, "Look, people are coming down from the navel of the land, and one division is coming by way of the oak of the diviners."
verses.9:38: Then Zebul said to him, "Where is your mouth now, with which you said, 'Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him?' Is not this the people whom you despised? Go out now, please, and fight them!"
verses.9:39: So Gaal went out before the lords of Shechem and fought against Abimelech.
verses.9:40: And Abimelech pursued him, and he fled before him, and many fell dead right up to the entrance of the gate.
verses.9:41: Then Abimelech lived at Arumah, and Zebul drove Gaal and his brothers out from living in Shechem.
verses.9:42: And on the next day, the people went out into the field, and they told Abimelech.
verses.9:43: So he took the people, divided them into three divisions, and lay in ambush in the field. When he looked, there the people were, coming out of the city; so he rose up against them and struck them down.
verses.9:44: Then Abimelech and the divisions that were with him rushed forward and stood at the entrance of the city gate, while the two divisions rushed against all who were in the field and struck them down.
verses.9:45: And Abimelech fought against the city all that day; he captured the city and killed the people who were in it, and he tore down the city and sowed it with salt.
verses.9:46: When all the lords of the Tower of Shechem heard of it, they entered the vault of the house of El-berith.
verses.9:47: And it was reported to Abimelech that all the lords of the Tower of Shechem had gathered together.
verses.9:48: So Abimelech went up to Mount Zalmon, he and all the people who were with him. And Abimelech took the axes in his hand, cut down a branch from the trees, lifted it up, and placed it on his shoulder; and he said to the people who were with him, "What you have seen me do, hurry and do like me!"
verses.9:49: So all the people also cut down each man his own branch and went after Abimelech, and they placed them against the vault and set the vault on fire over them. Thus all the people of the Tower of Shechem died as well, about a thousand men and women.
verses.9:50: Then Abimelech went to Thebez, encamped against Thebez, and captured it.
verses.9:51: Now there was a strong tower in the middle of the city, and all the men and women and all the lords of the city fled there, shut themselves in, and went up onto the roof of the tower.
verses.9:52: And Abimelech came up to the tower and fought against it, and he approached the entrance of the tower to burn it with fire.
verses.9:53: Then one woman threw an upper millstone onto Abimelech's head and shattered his skull.
verses.9:54: Quickly he called to the young man who carried his armor and said to him, "Draw your sword and put me to death, so that they do not say about me, 'A woman killed him.'" So his young man pierced him through, and he died.
verses.9:55: When the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, each man went to his own place.
verses.9:56: So God returned Abimelech's evil, which he had done to his father by killing his seventy brothers.
verses.9:57: And all the evil of the men of Shechem God returned upon their own heads, and the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.
verses.10:1: Following Abimelech, Tola son of Puah, son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, rose up to deliver Israel. He resided at Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.
verses.10:2: He judged Israel for twenty-three years; then he died and was buried at Shamir.
verses.10:3: After him, Jair the Gileadite rose up, and he judged Israel for twenty-two years.
verses.10:4: He had thirty sons riding on thirty donkey colts, and thirty towns belonged to them; to this very day those towns, which are in the land of Gilead, are called Havvoth-jair.
verses.10:5: Then Jair died and was buried at Kamon.
verses.10:6: Once more the sons of Israel did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD. They served the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and the gods of Aram, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the Ammonites, and the gods of the Philistines; they abandoned the LORD and did not serve Him.
verses.10:7: Then the LORD's anger burned against Israel, and He sold them into the hand of the Philistines and into the hand of the Ammonites.
verses.10:8: In that year they shattered and crushed the sons of Israel—for eighteen years, all the sons of Israel who were across the Jordan, in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead.
verses.10:9: Moreover, the Ammonites crossed the Jordan to fight against Judah as well, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, so that Israel was severely distressed.
verses.10:10: Then the sons of Israel cried out to the LORD, saying, "We have sinned against You, in that we abandoned our God and served the Baals."
verses.10:11: The LORD said to the sons of Israel, "Did I not deliver you from Egypt, and from the Amorites, and from the Ammonites, and from the Philistines?
verses.10:12: The Sidonians, Amalek, and Maon also oppressed you; you cried out to Me, and I delivered you from their hand.
verses.10:13: Yet you abandoned Me and served other gods; therefore I will not deliver you anymore.
verses.10:14: Go and cry out to the gods you have chosen; let them deliver you in your time of distress!"
verses.10:15: Then the sons of Israel said to the LORD, "We have sinned. You do to us according to everything that is good in Your eyes; only please rescue us this very day."
verses.10:16: So they removed the foreign gods from among them and served the LORD, and His soul could no longer endure Israel's misery.
verses.10:17: Then the Ammonites were called to arms and encamped in Gilead, while the sons of Israel assembled and encamped at Mizpah.
verses.10:18: The people, the leaders of Gilead, said to one another, "Who is the man who will begin to fight against the Ammonites? He will become head over all the residents of Gilead."
verses.11:1: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty fighting man, and he was the son of a prostitute; Gilead fathered Jephthah.
verses.11:2: Gilead's wife also bore him sons; when the wife's sons grew up, they drove Jephthah out and said to him, "You will not inherit in our father's house, because you are the son of another woman."
verses.11:3: So Jephthah fled from his brothers and settled in the land of Tob; worthless men gathered around Jephthah and went out with him.
verses.11:4: Some time later, the Ammonites went to war against Israel.
verses.11:5: And when the Ammonites fought against Israel, the elders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah from the land of Tob.
verses.11:6: They said to Jephthah, "Come and be our commander, so that we may fight against the Ammonites."
verses.11:7: Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "Was it not you who hated me and drove me away from my father's house? Why then have you come to me now that you are in distress?"
verses.11:8: The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "For that very reason we have turned back to you now: come with us and fight against the Ammonites, and you will become head for us, over all the residents of Gilead."
verses.11:9: Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "If you are bringing me back to fight against the Ammonites and the LORD gives them over before me, I myself will become your head."
verses.11:10: The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "The LORD will be listening between us: we will surely act just according to your word."
verses.11:11: So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people set him over themselves as head and commander. Then Jephthah spoke all his words before the LORD at Mizpah.
verses.11:12: Then Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites, saying, "What is between me and you, that you have come against me to fight in my land?"
verses.11:13: The king of the Ammonites answered Jephthah's messengers, "Because Israel took my land when it came up from Egypt, from the Arnon as far as the Jabbok and to the Jordan. Now then, restore them in peace."
verses.11:14: Once again Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the Ammonites.
verses.11:15: He said to him, "This is what Jephthah says: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the Ammonites.
verses.11:16: Instead, when they came up from Egypt, Israel marched through the wilderness as far as the Sea of Reeds and arrived at Kadesh.
verses.11:17: Then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, 'Please allow me to cross through your land,' but the king of Edom did not listen. They also sent to the king of Moab, and he was unwilling; so Israel stayed at Kadesh.
verses.11:18: Next they traveled through the wilderness, circled around the land of Edom and the land of Moab, arrived on the east side of the land of Moab, and encamped across the Arnon; they did not enter the territory of Moab, because the Arnon was the border of Moab.
verses.11:19: Israel then sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, king of Heshbon, and Israel said to him, 'Please let us cross through your land to my place.'
verses.11:20: Sihon, however, did not trust Israel to cross through his territory; so Sihon gathered all his people, they encamped at Jahaz, and he fought against Israel.
verses.11:21: Then the LORD, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and all his people into Israel's hand, and they struck them down; thus Israel took possession of the entire land of the Amorites who lived in that land.
verses.11:22: They took possession of all the territory of the Amorites, from the Arnon as far as the Jabbok, and from the wilderness as far as the Jordan.
verses.11:23: So now the LORD, the God of Israel, has dispossessed the Amorites before His people Israel, and should you possess it?
verses.11:24: What Chemosh your god causes you to possess, do you not possess that? And everything the LORD our God has dispossessed from before us, that we will possess.
verses.11:25: Now then, are you really any better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever contend with Israel, or did he ever fight against them?
verses.11:26: While Israel inhabited Heshbon and its villages, Aroer and its villages, and all the towns along the sides of the Arnon for three hundred years, why did you not reclaim them during that time?
verses.11:27: I myself have not sinned against you, yet you are doing me wrong by fighting against me. May the LORD, the Judge, judge today between the sons of Israel and the Ammonites."
verses.11:28: Yet the king of the Ammonites did not listen to the words of Jephthah that he had sent to him.
verses.11:29: Then the Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh; he also passed through Mizpeh of Gilead, and from Mizpeh of Gilead he crossed over to the Ammonites.
verses.11:30: Jephthah made a vow to the LORD and said, "If You indeed give the Ammonites into my hand,
verses.11:31: then the one who comes out from the doors of my house to meet me when I come back in peace from the Ammonites will belong to the LORD, and I will offer that one up as a burnt offering."
verses.11:32: So Jephthah crossed over to the Ammonites to fight against them, and the LORD gave them into his hand.
verses.11:33: He struck them down from Aroer until you reach Minnith—twenty towns—and as far as Abel-keramim, with a very severe blow. Thus the Ammonites were subdued before the sons of Israel.
verses.11:34: When Jephthah arrived at Mizpah, at his house, look—his daughter was coming out to meet him with tambourines and with dancing! Now she alone was his only child; he had no other son or daughter of his own.
verses.11:35: The moment he saw her, he tore his clothes and said, "Alas, my daughter! You have brought me completely to my knees, and you have become among those who trouble me; for I have opened my mouth to the LORD, and I cannot turn back."
verses.11:36: She said to him, "My father, you have opened your mouth to the LORD; do to me according to what has come out from your mouth, now that the LORD has carried out vengeance for you upon your enemies, the Ammonites."
verses.11:37: Then she said to her father, "Let this thing be done for me: leave me alone for two months, so that I may depart and go down onto the mountains and weep over my virginity, I and my companions."
verses.11:38: He said, "Go." So he sent her off for two months; she and her companions went, and she wept over her virginity on the mountains.
verses.11:39: At the end of two months she returned to her father, and he carried out on her his vow that he had vowed. She had never known a man. And it became a custom in Israel.
verses.11:40: Year by year the daughters of Israel would go to commemorate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite for four days each year.
verses.12:1: Then the men of Ephraim were summoned, and they crossed over to Zaphon and said to Jephthah, "Why did you cross over to fight against the sons of Ammon and did not call us to go with you? We will burn your house down over you with fire!"
verses.12:2: Jephthah said to them, "I and my people were in a severe dispute with the sons of Ammon, and I called out to you, yet you did not deliver me from their hand.
verses.12:3: When I saw that you were no deliverer, I placed my life in my hand and crossed over against the sons of Ammon, and the LORD gave them into my hand. Why then have you come up to me this day to fight against me?"
verses.12:4: Then Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead and fought with Ephraim; and the men of Gilead struck down Ephraim, because they had said, "You are fugitives of Ephraim, Gilead, in the midst of Ephraim, in the midst of Manasseh."
verses.12:5: And Gilead captured the fords of the Jordan against Ephraim. And it happened that whenever any of the fugitives of Ephraim said, "Let me cross over," the men of Gilead would say to him, "Are you an Ephraimite?" And he would say, "No."
verses.12:6: Then they would say to him, "Please say 'Shibboleth.'" And he would say, "Sibboleth," for he could not manage to pronounce it right. Then they would seize him and slaughter him at the fords of the Jordan. So forty-two thousand from Ephraim fell at that time.
verses.12:7: Jephthah judged Israel for six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died, and he was buried among the cities of Gilead.
verses.12:8: And after him, Ibzan from Bethlehem judged Israel.
verses.12:9: He had thirty sons; he sent thirty daughters outside, and he brought thirty daughters in from outside for his sons. And he judged Israel for seven years.
verses.12:10: And Ibzan died, and he was buried in Bethlehem.
verses.12:11: And after him, Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel; and he judged Israel for ten years.
verses.12:12: And Elon the Zebulunite died, and he was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.
verses.12:13: And after him, Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel.
verses.12:14: He had forty sons and thirty grandsons who rode on seventy young donkeys; and he judged Israel for eight years.
verses.12:15: And Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite died, and he was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.
verses.13:1: Now the sons of Israel again did what was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD gave them into the hand of the Philistines for forty years.
verses.13:2: There was a certain man from Zorah, of the clan of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; and his wife was barren and had not given birth.
verses.13:3: And the angel of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, "Look now, you are barren and have not given birth, yet you will conceive and give birth to a son.
verses.13:4: So now, please be careful, and do not drink wine or strong drink, nor eat anything unclean.
verses.13:5: For look, you will conceive and give birth to a son, and no razor shall come up on his head, for the boy shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb. And he himself will begin to deliver Israel from the hand of the Philistines."
verses.13:6: Then the woman came and spoke to her husband, saying, "A man of God came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of the angel of God, exceedingly awesome. I did not ask him where he was from, nor did he tell me his name.
verses.13:7: But he said to me, 'Look, you will conceive and give birth to a son. So now, do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat any unclean thing, for the boy shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb until the day of his death.'"
verses.13:8: Then Manoah pleaded with the LORD and said, "Please, Lord, let the man of God whom You sent come to us again and teach us what we should do for the boy who is to be born."
verses.13:9: And God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the angel of God came again to the woman while she was sitting in the field, and Manoah her husband was not with her.
verses.13:10: So the woman hurried and ran and told her husband, and she said to him, "Look, the man who came to me on that day has appeared to me."
verses.13:11: Then Manoah arose and went after his wife, and he came to the man and said to him, "Are you the man who spoke to the woman?" And he said, "I am."
verses.13:12: Manoah said, "Now may your words come to pass! What shall be the rule for the boy, and his work?"
verses.13:13: And the angel of the LORD said to Manoah, "Let her be on guard concerning all that I said to the woman.
verses.13:14: She shall not eat of anything that comes from the grapevine, nor shall she drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing; everything that I commanded her, she shall keep."
verses.13:15: Then Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, "Please let us detain you, and let us prepare a young goat before you."
verses.13:16: And the angel of the LORD said to Manoah, "Even if you detain me, I will not eat of your food; and if you prepare a burnt offering, you must offer it up to the LORD." For Manoah did not know that he was the angel of the LORD.
verses.13:17: Manoah said to the angel of the LORD, "What is your name, so that when your word comes to pass we may honor you?"
verses.13:18: And the angel of the LORD said to him, "Why is it that you ask for my name, since it is wonderful?"
verses.13:19: So Manoah took the young goat and the grain offering and offered them up on the rock to the LORD, and he did a wondrous thing while Manoah and his wife were watching.
verses.13:20: And it happened that when the flame ascended from the altar toward heaven, the angel of the LORD ascended in the flame of the altar. While Manoah and his wife were watching, they fell on their faces to the ground.
verses.13:21: And the angel of the LORD never again appeared to Manoah or to his wife. Then Manoah knew that he was the angel of the LORD.
verses.13:22: So Manoah said to his wife, "We will surely die, because we have seen God!"
verses.13:23: But his wife said to him, "If the LORD had desired to put us to death, He would not have accepted a burnt offering and a grain offering from our hand, nor would He have shown us all these things, nor would He at this time have let us hear such a thing."
verses.13:24: Then the woman gave birth to a son and called his name Samson; and the boy grew up, and the LORD blessed him.
verses.13:25: And the Spirit of the LORD began to stir him in Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.
verses.14:1: Then Samson went down to Timnah, and he saw a woman in Timnah from the daughters of the Philistines.
verses.14:2: So he went up and told his father and his mother, saying, "I saw a woman in Timnah from the daughters of the Philistines; so now, get her for me as a wife."
verses.14:3: Then his father and his mother said to him, "Is there no woman among the daughters of your relatives, or among all my people, that you are going to take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?" But Samson said to his father, "Get her for me, because she is right in my eyes."
verses.14:4: Yet his father and his mother did not know that this was from the LORD, because He was seeking a pretext against the Philistines; and at that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel.
verses.14:5: Then Samson and his father and his mother went down to Timnah, and they came as far as the vineyards of Timnah; and look, a young lion came roaring toward him.
verses.14:6: And the Spirit of the LORD surged upon him, and he tore it apart as one tears apart a young goat, though there was nothing in his hand. Yet he did not tell his father or his mother what he had done.
verses.14:7: Then he went down and spoke to the woman, and she was right in the eyes of Samson.
verses.14:8: After some days he returned to take her, and he turned aside to look at the carcass of the lion; and look, a swarm of bees was in the body of the lion, along with honey.
verses.14:9: So he scraped it out into his palms and went along, eating as he walked. Then he went to his father and his mother and gave some to them, and they ate; yet he did not tell them that he had scraped the honey out from the body of the lion.
verses.14:10: Then his father went down to the woman, and Samson made a feast there, because that is what the young men used to do.
verses.14:11: And it happened that when they saw him, they brought thirty companions, and they were with him.
verses.14:12: Then Samson said to them, "Let me now pose a riddle to you: if you surely tell it to me within the seven days of the feast and find it out, then I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing.
verses.14:13: But if you are unable to tell me, then you yourselves shall give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing." And they said to him, "Pose your riddle, that we may hear it."
verses.14:14: So he said to them, "From the eater came forth food, and from the strong came forth what is sweet." And for three days they were unable to tell the riddle.
verses.14:15: And it happened on the seventh day that they said to Samson's wife, "Entice your husband so that he tells us the riddle, or else we will burn you and your father's house with fire. Was it to impoverish us that you invited us? Is it not so?"
verses.14:16: Then Samson's wife wept before him and said, "You only hate me and do not love me! You have posed a riddle to the sons of my people, yet you have not told it to me." And he said to her, "Look, I have not told my father or my mother, so should I tell you?"
verses.14:17: Yet she wept before him during the seven days that their feast lasted. And it happened on the seventh day that he told her, because she pressed him hard; then she told the riddle to the sons of her people.
verses.14:18: So on the seventh day, before the sun went down, the men of the city said to him, "What is sweeter than honey? And what is stronger than a lion?" And he said to them, "Had you not plowed with my heifer, you would not have found my riddle."
verses.14:19: Then the Spirit of the LORD surged upon him, and he went down to Ashkelon and struck down thirty men from among them, and took their spoil and gave the changes of clothing to those who had told the riddle. And his anger burned, and he went up to his father's house.
verses.14:20: And Samson's wife came to belong to his companion who had acted as his friend.
verses.15:1: Now it came about after some days, during the days of the wheat harvest, that Samson visited his wife with a young goat and said, "Let me go in to my wife in the inner room." But her father did not permit him to go in.
verses.15:2: Her father said, "I surely thought that you utterly hated her, so I gave her to your companion. Is not her younger sister better than she? Please let her be yours in her place."
verses.15:3: Samson said to them, "I am clear of guilt toward the Philistines this time when I do harm to them."
verses.15:4: Samson went and caught three hundred foxes. He took torches, turned them tail to tail, and placed one torch in the middle between every two tails.
verses.15:5: He kindled fire in the torches and sent them into the standing grain of the Philistines, and he burned up stacked grain and standing grain alike, as well as olive groves.
verses.15:6: Then the Philistines asked, "Who did this?" And they answered, "Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he took his wife and gave her to his companion." So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father with fire.
verses.15:7: Samson said to them, "If this is how you act, I will certainly take vengeance on you, and after that I will stop."
verses.15:8: He struck them leg upon thigh with a great blow; then he went down and settled in the cleft of the rock of Etam.
verses.15:9: Then the Philistines went up, encamped in Judah, and spread out in Lehi.
verses.15:10: The men of Judah asked, "Why have you come up against us?" They answered, "We have come up to bind Samson, to do to him just as he did to us."
verses.15:11: So three thousand men from Judah went down to the cleft of the rock of Etam and said to Samson, "Do you not know that the Philistines rule over us? And what is this you have done to us?" He said to them, "Just as they did to me, so I have done to them."
verses.15:12: They said to him, "We have come down to bind you, to give you into the hand of the Philistines." Samson said to them, "Swear to me that you yourselves will not fall upon me."
verses.15:13: They spoke to him, saying, "No, rather we will surely bind you and give you into their hand, yet we will certainly not put you to death." So they bound him with two new ropes and brought him up from the rock.
verses.15:14: When he came to Lehi, the Philistines shouted to meet him. Then the Spirit of the LORD surged upon him, and the ropes that were on his arms became like flax that has burned in fire, and his bonds melted off his hands.
verses.15:15: He found a fresh jawbone of a donkey, reached out his hand and took it, and struck down a thousand men with it.
verses.15:16: Then Samson said, "With the jawbone of a donkey, one heap, two heaps; with the jawbone of a donkey, I have struck down a thousand men."
verses.15:17: When he had finished speaking, he threw the jawbone from his hand, and he called that place Ramath-lehi.
verses.15:18: Then he became very thirsty, and he called to the LORD and said, "You have given this great deliverance by the hand of Your servant; and now shall I die of thirst and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?"
verses.15:19: So God split open the hollow basin that is in Lehi, and water came out of it. He drank, and his spirit returned and he revived. Therefore he called its name En-hakkore, which is in Lehi to this day.
verses.15:20: And he judged Israel in the days of the Philistines for twenty years.
verses.16:1: Samson went to Gaza, and there he saw a prostitute, and he went in to her.
verses.16:2: It was reported to the Gazites, saying, "Samson has come here." So they encircled him and lay in ambush for him all night at the gate of the city. They kept silent all night, saying, "Until the light of morning—then we will kill him."
verses.16:3: Samson lay until midnight, and at midnight he got up, grasped the doors of the city gate and the two posts, pulled them up along with the bar, put them on his shoulders, and carried them up to the top of the mountain that faces Hebron.
verses.16:4: Afterward it happened that he loved a woman in the Valley of Sorek, and her name was Delilah.
verses.16:5: The lords of the Philistines went up to her and said to her, "Entice him and see where his great strength lies and how we may overpower him, so that we may bind him to subdue him; and each of us will give you eleven hundred pieces of silver."
verses.16:6: So Delilah said to Samson, "Please tell me where your great strength lies, and with what you could be bound to subdue you."
verses.16:7: Samson told her, "If they bind me with seven fresh bowstrings that have not been dried, then I will become weak and be like any other man."
verses.16:8: Then the lords of the Philistines brought up to her seven fresh bowstrings that had not been dried, and she bound him with them.
verses.16:9: Now men in ambush were waiting for her in the inner room. She said to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" But he snapped the bowstrings just as a strand of tow snaps when it smells fire. So his strength was not known.
verses.16:10: Then Delilah said to Samson, "Look, you have mocked me and spoken lies to me. Now please tell me with what you can be bound."
verses.16:11: He said to her, "If they bind me fast with new ropes with which no work has been done, then I will become weak and be like any other man."
verses.16:12: So Delilah took new ropes and bound him with them, and she said to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" Meanwhile, the men in ambush were waiting in the inner room. But he snapped them off his arms like a thread.
verses.16:13: Then Delilah said to Samson, "Up to now you have mocked me and spoken lies to me. Tell me with what you can be bound." And he said to her, "If you weave the seven braids of my head with the web."
verses.16:14: So she fastened them with the pin and said to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" He awoke from his sleep and pulled up the pin of the loom and the web.
verses.16:15: Then she said to him, "How can you say, 'I love you,' when your heart is not with me? These three times you have mocked me and have not told me where your great strength lies."
verses.16:16: And it came about, when she pressed him with her words every day and urged him, that his soul grew weary to death.
verses.16:17: So he told her all his heart and said to her, "A razor has never come upon my head, for I have been a Nazirite to God from my mother's womb. If I am shaved, my strength will depart from me, and I will become weak and be like all other men."
verses.16:18: When Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart, she sent and called for the lords of the Philistines, saying, "Come up this one time, for he has told me all his heart." Then the lords of the Philistines came up to her and brought up the silver in their hands.
verses.16:19: She made him sleep on her knees, and she called for a man and shaved off the seven braids of his head. Then she began to subdue him, and his strength departed from him.
verses.16:20: She said, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" He awoke from his sleep and said, "I will go out as at other times and shake myself free." But he did not know that the LORD had departed from him.
verses.16:21: Then the Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes. They brought him down to Gaza and bound him with bronze shackles, and he was grinding in the prison house.
verses.16:22: Yet the hair of his head began to grow back after he was shaved.
verses.16:23: Now the lords of the Philistines assembled to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god and to rejoice, and they said, "Our god has given Samson our enemy into our hand."
verses.16:24: When the people saw him, they praised their god, for they said, "Our god has given into our hand our enemy, the devastator of our land, and the one who multiplied our dead."
verses.16:25: When their hearts were merry, they said, "Call for Samson, so that he may entertain us." So they called Samson out of the prison house, and he entertained before them. Then they stationed him between the pillars.
verses.16:26: Then Samson said to the young man who held him by the hand, "Let go of me, and let me feel the pillars on which the house rests, so that I may lean against them."
verses.16:27: Now the house was full of men and women, and all the lords of the Philistines were there. And on the roof were about three thousand men and women watching Samson entertain.
verses.16:28: Then Samson called to the LORD and said, "Lord GOD, please remember me and please strengthen me just this once, God, so that I may be avenged on the Philistines for one of my two eyes."
verses.16:29: And Samson grasped the two middle pillars on which the house rested, and he braced himself against them, one with his right hand and one with his left.
verses.16:30: And Samson said, "Let my soul die with the Philistines!" Then he bent forward with strength, and the house fell upon the lords and upon all the people who were in it. So the dead whom he put to death in his death were more than those he had put to death in his life.
verses.16:31: Then his brothers and all his father's household went down and carried him, and they went up and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of Manoah his father. He had judged Israel for twenty years.
verses.17:1: Now there was a man from the hill country of Ephraim, and his name was Micah.
verses.17:2: He said to his mother, "The eleven hundred pieces of silver that were taken from you, over which you uttered a curse and also spoke in my ears—look, the silver is with me; I myself took it." And his mother said, "Blessed be my son by the LORD."
verses.17:3: So he returned the eleven hundred pieces of silver to his mother, and his mother said, "I wholly dedicate the silver to the LORD from my hand for my son, to make a carved image and a cast image; so now I will return it to you."
verses.17:4: So when he returned the silver to his mother, his mother took two hundred pieces of silver and gave them to the silversmith, and he made them into a carved image and a cast image, and it was in the house of Micah.
verses.17:5: Now the man Micah had a house of gods, and he made an ephod and teraphim, and he installed one of his sons, and he became his priest.
verses.17:6: In those days there was no king in Israel; each man would do what was right in his own eyes.
verses.17:7: Now there was a young man from Bethlehem in Judah, of the clan of Judah, who was a Levite and was sojourning there.
verses.17:8: Then the man departed from the city, from Bethlehem in Judah, to sojourn wherever he could find a place; and he came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, as he made his way.
