verses.17:9: Micah asked him, "Where do you come from?" He answered him, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I am going to sojourn wherever I can find a place."
verses.17:10: Then Micah said to him, "Stay with me and be a father and a priest to me, and I will give you ten pieces of silver a year, a set of garments, and your sustenance." So the Levite went in.
verses.17:11: The Levite agreed to stay with the man, and the young man became to him like one of his sons.
verses.17:12: So Micah installed the Levite, and the young man became his priest and remained in the house of Micah.
verses.17:13: Then Micah said, "Now I know that the LORD will do good to me, because the Levite has become my priest."
verses.18:1: In those days there was no king in Israel, and in those days the tribe of the Danites was seeking for itself an inheritance in which to dwell, because up to that day nothing had fallen to it as an inheritance among the tribes of Israel.
verses.18:2: So the sons of Dan sent from their clan five men out of their whole number, men of valor from Zorah and from Eshtaol, to spy out the land and to explore it; and they said to them, "Go, explore the land." And they came to the hill country of Ephraim, up to the house of Micah, and spent the night there.
verses.18:3: While they were near the house of Micah, they recognized the voice of the young Levite; so they turned aside there and said to him, "Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place, and what do you have here?"
verses.18:4: He said to them, "Micah has done such and such for me; he hired me, and I have become his priest."
verses.18:5: They said to him, "Please inquire of God so that we may know whether our way, on which we are going, will succeed."
verses.18:6: The priest said to them, "Go in peace. Your way on which you are going is directly before the LORD."
verses.18:7: Then the five men went and came to Laish, and saw the people who were in its midst dwelling in security, according to the custom of the Sidonians, quiet and unsuspecting; and there was no possessor of authority in the land humiliating anyone in any matter, and they were far from the Sidonians and had no dealings with anyone.
verses.18:8: They came to their brothers at Zorah and Eshtaol, and their brothers said to them, "What do you have to say?"
verses.18:9: They said, "Arise, and let us go up against them; for we have seen the land, and look, it is very good! And you are sitting still! Do not be sluggish to go, to enter to take possession of the land.
verses.18:10: When you enter, you will come to an unsuspecting people, and the land is spacious; for God has given it into your hand, a place where there is no lack of anything that is on the earth."
verses.18:11: Then they set out from there, from the clan of the Danites, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, six hundred men armed with weapons of war.
verses.18:12: They went up and encamped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. Therefore they have called that place Mahaneh-dan to this day; look, it is behind Kiriath-jearim.
verses.18:13: And they passed on from there to the hill country of Ephraim, and came as far as the house of Micah.
verses.18:14: Then the five men who had gone to spy out the land of Laish spoke up and said to their brothers, "Do you know that in these houses there are an ephod and teraphim, and a carved image and a cast image? Now then, consider what you should do."
verses.18:15: So they turned aside there and came to the house of the young Levite, the house of Micah, and inquired about his welfare.
verses.18:16: Now the six hundred men who were from the sons of Dan, armed with their weapons of war, were standing at the entrance of the gate.
verses.18:17: And the five men who had gone to spy out the land went up, entered there, and took the carved image, the ephod, the teraphim, and the cast image, while the priest was standing at the entrance of the gate with the six hundred men who were armed with the weapons of war.
verses.18:18: When these entered the house of Micah and took the carved image of the ephod, the teraphim, and the cast image, the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"
verses.18:19: They said to him, "Keep quiet, put your hand over your mouth, and go with us, and be a father and a priest to us. Is it better for you to be a priest for the house of one man, or for you to be a priest for a tribe and a clan in Israel?"
verses.18:20: The priest's heart was glad, so he took the ephod, the teraphim, and the carved image, and went into the midst of the people.
verses.18:21: Then they turned and went, and they placed the little ones, the livestock, and the baggage ahead of them.
verses.18:22: When they had gone far from the house of Micah, the men who were in the houses beside the house of Micah rallied together and overtook the sons of Dan.
verses.18:23: They called out to the sons of Dan, who turned their faces around and said to Micah, "What is the matter with you, that you have rallied?"
verses.18:24: He said, "You have taken my gods that I made, and the priest, and have gone away; and what do I have left? And how is it that you say to me, 'What is the matter with you?'"
verses.18:25: The sons of Dan said to him, "Do not let your voice be heard among us, or else men bitter of soul may fall upon you, and you will lose your life and the lives of your household."
verses.18:26: And the sons of Dan went on their way; and Micah saw that they were stronger than he, so he turned and went back to his house.
verses.18:27: So they took what Micah had made, and the priest who had belonged to him, and came upon Laish, upon a quiet and unsuspecting people, and struck them with the edge of the sword; and they burned the city with fire.
verses.18:28: And there was no deliverer, because it was far from Sidon and they had no dealings with anyone, and it was in the valley that belongs to Beth-rehob. Then they rebuilt the city and lived in it.
verses.18:29: And they called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born to Israel; however, Laish was the name of the city at first.
verses.18:30: And the sons of Dan set up the carved image for themselves; and Jonathan the son of Gershom, the son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of the Danites until the day of the exile of the land.
verses.18:31: So they established for themselves Micah's carved image that he had made, all the days that the house of God was in Shiloh.
verses.19:1: Now it happened in those days, when there was no king in Israel, that there was a Levite man sojourning in the remote parts of the hill country of Ephraim, who took a concubine for himself from Bethlehem in Judah.
verses.19:2: But his concubine acted unfaithfully against him, and went away from him to her father's house, to Bethlehem in Judah; and she was there for a period of four months.
verses.19:3: Then her husband arose and went after her to speak to her heart, to bring her back; his attendant was with him, along with a pair of donkeys. She brought him into her father's house, and when the father of the young woman saw him, he rejoiced to meet him.
verses.19:4: His father-in-law, the father of the young woman, detained him, so he stayed with him three days; they ate and drank and spent the night there.
verses.19:5: On the fourth day they got up early in the morning, and he arose to go; but the father of the young woman said to his son-in-law, "Sustain your heart with a piece of bread, and afterward you may go."
verses.19:6: So they sat down, and the two of them ate and drank together; and the father of the young woman said to the man, "Please agree and spend the night, and let your heart be glad."
verses.19:7: When the man arose to go, his father-in-law urged him insistently, so he turned back and spent the night there.
verses.19:8: On the fifth day he got up early in the morning to go, and the father of the young woman said, "Please sustain your heart, and linger until the day declines." So the two of them ate.
verses.19:9: Then the man arose to go, he and his concubine and his attendant; but his father-in-law, the father of the young woman, said to him, "Look now, the day has waned toward evening; please spend the night. See, the day is drawing to a close; spend the night here and let your heart be glad. Tomorrow you may rise early for your way and go to your tent."
verses.19:10: But the man was not willing to spend the night, so he arose and went, and came opposite Jebus, that is, Jerusalem. With him was a pair of saddled donkeys, and his concubine was with him.
verses.19:11: When they were near Jebus, the day had gone far down; and the attendant said to his master, "Please come, let us turn aside into this city of the Jebusites and spend the night in it."
verses.19:12: His master said to him, "We will not turn aside into a city of foreigners, who are not of the sons of Israel; we will pass on as far as Gibeah."
verses.19:13: And he said to his attendant, "Come, let us draw near to one of the places, and spend the night in Gibeah or in Ramah."
verses.19:14: So they passed on and went, and the sun went down on them beside Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin.
verses.19:15: They turned aside there to go in to spend the night in Gibeah. He went in and sat down in the open square of the city, and there was no one taking them into a house to spend the night.
verses.19:16: Then look, an old man was coming from his work out of the field in the evening. Now the man was from the hill country of Ephraim, and he was sojourning in Gibeah; but the men of the place were Benjaminites.
verses.19:17: He lifted up his eyes and saw the traveling man in the open square of the city; and the old man said, "Where are you going, and where are you coming from?"
verses.19:18: He said to him, "We are passing through from Bethlehem in Judah to the remote parts of the hill country of Ephraim. I am from there, and I went to Bethlehem in Judah; now I am going to the house of the LORD, yet there is no one taking me into a house.
verses.19:19: Yet there is both straw and fodder for our donkeys, and also bread and wine for me, for your maidservant, and for the attendant who is with your servants; there is no lack of anything."
verses.19:20: The old man said, "Peace to you! Only let all that you lack be upon me; only do not spend the night in the open square."
verses.19:21: So he brought him into his house and gave fodder to the donkeys; and they washed their feet, and ate and drank.
verses.19:22: While they were making their hearts glad, look, the men of the city, men who were sons of worthlessness, surrounded the house, pounding on the door; and they spoke to the old man, the owner of the house, saying, "Bring out the man who came into your house, so that we may know him."
verses.19:23: Then the man, the owner of the house, went out to them and said to them, "No, my brothers, please do not act wickedly! Since this man has come into my house, do not commit this outrage.
verses.19:24: Here are my virgin daughter and his concubine; please let me bring them out, and violate them and do to them what is good in your eyes, but to this man you must not do this outrageous thing."
verses.19:25: But the men were not willing to listen to him. So the man seized his concubine and brought her outside to them; and they knew her and abused her all night until the morning, and let her go as the dawn was rising.
verses.19:26: And the woman came as morning approached, and fell at the entrance of the house of the man where her master was, until daylight.
verses.19:27: When her master arose in the morning, opened the doors of the house, and went out to go on his way, look, the woman, his concubine, was lying fallen at the entrance of the house, with her hands on the threshold.
verses.19:28: He said to her, "Get up, and let us go." But there was no answer. So he took her up onto the donkey, and the man arose and went to his place.
verses.19:29: When he came into his house, he took the knife, seized his concubine, and cut her up by her bones into twelve pieces, and sent her throughout all the territory of Israel.
verses.19:30: And it came about that everyone who saw it said, "Nothing like this has happened or been seen from the day the sons of Israel came up from the land of Egypt until this day. Set your minds to it, take counsel, and speak!"
verses.20:1: All the sons of Israel went out, and the congregation assembled as one man, from Dan even to Beersheba and the land of Gilead, to the LORD at Mizpah.
verses.20:2: And the chiefs of all the people, all the tribes of Israel, took their stand in the assembly of the people of God: four hundred thousand men on foot who drew a sword.
verses.20:3: Now the sons of Benjamin heard that the sons of Israel had gone up to Mizpah. And the sons of Israel said, "Speak, how did this evil happen?"
verses.20:4: Then the Levite man, the husband of the murdered woman, answered and said, "I and my concubine came to Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin, to spend the night.
verses.20:5: The citizens of Gibeah rose up against me and surrounded the house against me by night. They intended to kill me, and they violated my concubine, and she died.
verses.20:6: So I took hold of my concubine, cut her into pieces, and sent her throughout the whole territory of Israel's inheritance, because they committed depravity and outrage in Israel.
verses.20:7: Look, all of you are sons of Israel; give your word and counsel here."
verses.20:8: Then all the people rose up as one man, saying, "Not one of us will go to his tent, and not one of us will turn back to his house.
verses.20:9: And now this is the thing we will do to Gibeah: against it by lot.
verses.20:10: We will take ten men out of a hundred throughout all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred out of a thousand, and a thousand out of ten thousand, to fetch provisions for the people, so that when they come to Geba of Benjamin, they may act according to all the outrage it has committed in Israel."
verses.20:11: So all the men of Israel gathered against the city as one man, united together.
verses.20:12: Then the tribes of Israel sent men throughout all the tribes of Benjamin, saying, "What is this evil that has happened among you?
verses.20:13: Now then, hand over the men, the worthless fellows who are in Gibeah, so that we may put them to death and purge evil from Israel." But the sons of Benjamin were not willing to listen to the voice of their brothers, the sons of Israel.
verses.20:14: And the sons of Benjamin gathered from the cities to Gibeah to go out to battle against the sons of Israel.
verses.20:15: And on that day the sons of Benjamin were mustered from the cities: twenty-six thousand men who drew a sword, besides the inhabitants of Gibeah, who were mustered as seven hundred picked men.
verses.20:16: Out of all these people, seven hundred picked men were left-handed; every one of them could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.
verses.20:17: And the men of Israel, apart from Benjamin, were mustered: four hundred thousand men who drew a sword; all of these were men of war.
verses.20:18: Then they arose and went up to Bethel and inquired of God, and the sons of Israel said, "Who shall go up for us first to battle against the sons of Benjamin?" And the LORD said, "Judah first."
verses.20:19: So the sons of Israel arose in the morning and encamped against Gibeah.
verses.20:20: Then the men of Israel went out to battle against Benjamin, and the men of Israel drew up battle lines against them facing Gibeah.
verses.20:21: And the sons of Benjamin came out from Gibeah and on that day destroyed twenty-two thousand men of Israel down to the ground.
verses.20:22: But the people, the men of Israel, strengthened themselves and once more drew up battle lines in the place where they had drawn up on the first day.
verses.20:23: And the sons of Israel went up and wept before the LORD until evening, and they inquired of the LORD, saying, "Shall I draw near again to battle against the sons of my brother Benjamin?" And the LORD said, "Go up against him."
verses.20:24: So the sons of Israel came near to the sons of Benjamin on the second day.
verses.20:25: And Benjamin came out from Gibeah to meet them on the second day, and they destroyed another eighteen thousand men of the sons of Israel down to the ground; all of these drew a sword.
verses.20:26: Then all the sons of Israel and all the people went up and came to Bethel, and they wept and sat there before the LORD, and fasted that day until evening, and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.
verses.20:27: And the sons of Israel inquired of the LORD—for the ark of the covenant of God was there in those days,
verses.20:28: and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, was standing before it in those days—saying, "Shall I still go out again to battle against the sons of my brother Benjamin, or shall I stop?" And the LORD said, "Go up, for tomorrow I will give him into your hand."
verses.20:29: So Israel set men in ambush all around Gibeah.
verses.20:30: And the sons of Israel went up against the sons of Benjamin on the third day and drew up in formation against Gibeah, as at the previous times.
verses.20:31: Then the sons of Benjamin came out to meet the people and were drawn away from the city; and they began to strike down and kill some of the people, as at the previous times, on the highways—one of which goes up to Bethel and the other to Gibeah—in the open field, about thirty men of Israel.
verses.20:32: And the sons of Benjamin said, "They are being defeated before us as at the first." But the sons of Israel had said, "Let us flee and draw them away from the city to the highways."
verses.20:33: Then all the men of Israel rose from their place and drew up in formation at Baal-tamar; and Israel's ambush rushed out from its place, from the open ground of Geba.
verses.20:34: And ten thousand picked men out of all Israel came from opposite Gibeah, and the battle was heavy; yet they did not know that disaster was closing in on them.
verses.20:35: And the LORD defeated Benjamin before Israel, and on that day the sons of Israel destroyed twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Benjamin; all of these drew a sword.
verses.20:36: So the sons of Benjamin saw that they were defeated. Now the men of Israel gave ground to Benjamin because they relied on the ambush that they had set against Gibeah.
verses.20:37: And the ambush hurried and rushed upon Gibeah; and the ambush spread out and struck the entire city with the edge of the sword.
verses.20:38: Now the men of Israel had an appointed signal with the ambush: that they would send up a great signal plume of smoke from the city.
verses.20:39: Then the men of Israel turned about in the battle. Now Benjamin had begun to strike down and kill about thirty men among the men of Israel, for they said, "Surely they are completely defeated before us, as in the first battle."
verses.20:40: But the signal plume began to rise from the city, a pillar of smoke. And Benjamin looked behind him, and look, the entire city was rising into the sky.
verses.20:41: Then the men of Israel turned about, and the men of Benjamin were terrified, for they saw that disaster had closed in on them.
verses.20:42: So they turned away before the men of Israel toward the way of the wilderness, but the battle overtook them, and those from the cities were destroying them in their midst.
verses.20:43: They encircled Benjamin, pursued them, and trod them down at their resting place, as far as opposite Gibeah on the east.
verses.20:44: So eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell; all of these were men of valor.
verses.20:45: And they turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, and they gleaned five thousand men of them on the highways; and they pressed closely after them as far as Gidom and struck down two thousand men of them.
verses.20:46: So all who fell from Benjamin on that day were twenty-five thousand men who drew a sword; all of these were men of valor.
verses.20:47: But six hundred men turned and fled toward the wilderness to the rock of Rimmon, and they remained at the rock of Rimmon for four months.
verses.20:48: And the men of Israel turned back against the sons of Benjamin and struck them with the edge of the sword, from the entire city to the livestock, to everything that was found; moreover, all the cities that were found they set on fire.
verses.21:1: Now the men of Israel had sworn at Mizpah, saying, "No man among us will give his daughter to Benjamin as a wife."
verses.21:2: And the people came to Bethel and sat there until evening before God; they raised their voices and wept with great weeping.
verses.21:3: And they said, "Why, LORD, God of Israel, has this happened in Israel, so that one tribe is missing from Israel today?"
verses.21:4: Then on the next day the people rose early, built an altar there, and offered up burnt offerings and peace offerings.
verses.21:5: And the sons of Israel said, "Who is it among all the tribes of Israel who did not go up in the assembly to the LORD?" For the great oath had been made concerning anyone who did not go up to the LORD at Mizpah, saying, "He will certainly be put to death."
verses.21:6: And the sons of Israel felt sorrow for Benjamin their brother and said, "Today one tribe has been cut off from Israel.
verses.21:7: What should we do for wives for them, for those who remain, since we have sworn by the LORD not to give any of our daughters to them as wives?"
verses.21:8: Then they said, "Which one from the tribes of Israel did not go up to the LORD at Mizpah?" And look, not a man from Jabesh-gilead had come to the camp, to the assembly.
verses.21:9: The people were mustered, and look, not a man from the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead was there.
verses.21:10: So the congregation sent there twelve thousand men from the brave warriors and commanded them, saying, "Go and strike down the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead by the edge of the sword, along with the women and the little ones.
verses.21:11: And this is the thing that you are to do: every male and every woman who has known lying with a male you must devote to destruction."
verses.21:12: And they found from among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead four hundred young virgin women who had not known a man by lying with a male, and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.
verses.21:13: So the entire congregation sent word and spoke to the sons of Benjamin who were at the rock of Rimmon, and declared peace to them.
verses.21:14: At that time Benjamin returned, and they gave them the women whom they had kept alive from among the women of Jabesh-gilead; yet even so they did not suffice for them.
verses.21:15: Now the people felt sorrow for Benjamin, because the LORD had made a breach among the tribes of Israel.
verses.21:16: So the elders of the congregation said, "What should we do for wives for those who remain, since the women have been wiped out from Benjamin?"
verses.21:17: And they said, "Benjamin's surviving remnant must have an inheritance, so that no tribe is blotted out from Israel.
verses.21:18: Yet we are not able to give them wives from among our daughters." For the sons of Israel had sworn, saying, "Cursed is whoever gives a wife to Benjamin."
verses.21:19: Then they said, "Look, from year to year there is a festival of the LORD in Shiloh, which lies to the north of Bethel, east of the highway that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and to the south of Lebonah."
verses.21:20: Then they commanded the sons of Benjamin, saying, "Go and wait in ambush in the vineyards,
verses.21:21: and watch. Look, if the daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in the dances, then come out from the vineyards and seize for yourselves, each man his wife, from the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.
verses.21:22: And it will happen, when their fathers or their brothers come to contend with us, that we will say to them, 'Graciously give them to us, because we did not take for each man his wife in the war, and because it was not you who gave them to them; otherwise you would now be guilty.'"
verses.21:23: And the sons of Benjamin did just so: they took wives according to their number from the dancing women whom they had carried off, and they went and returned to their inheritance, rebuilt the cities, and settled in them.
verses.21:24: And at that time the sons of Israel went their way from there, each man to his tribe and to his clan; and they went out from there, each man to his inheritance.
verses.21:25: In those days there was no king in Israel; each man would do what was right in his eyes.

notes.1:14: The rare Qal verb tsanach ("dismounted") occurs only here, Joshua 15:18, and Judges 4:21; paired with "from upon the donkey," it denotes getting down or alighting from a mount.
notes.1:19: Both "took possession of" (vayyoresh) and "to dispossess" (lehorish) are Hiphil forms of yarash, denoting taking possession of territory and dispossessing inhabitants respectively. The construction lo followed by le- plus an infinitive construct expresses inability ("could not dispossess").
notes.1:23: "Had Bethel scouted out" reflects the rare Hiphil stem of tur (usually Qal, "spy out"), expressing causative reconnaissance. In verse 24, "lookouts" translates the Qal participle shomerim ("watchers, guards").
notes.1:27: Translates the Qere yoshevei ("the inhabitants of," plural construct, matching Ibleam and Megiddo) rather than the Ketiv yoshev (singular construct, "the inhabitant of"). "Daughter towns" renders the Hebrew idiom benoteiha (literally "its daughters"), denoting dependent satellite villages.
notes.2:1: The Hiphil imperfect (yiqtol) a'aleh ("I brought you up") followed by the wayyiqtol va'avi ("and brought you") uses a vivid or archaic past yiqtol to recount the historical deliverance from Egypt. "Bochim" (ha-Bokhim) is the Qal masculine plural participle of bakhah, literally "the Weepers," linking to verses 4-5.
notes.2:3: "Thorns in your sides" renders the concise Masoretic reading letsiddim (literally "for sides"), traditionally understood as an ellipsis of the idiom "thorns in your sides" or "a scourge in your sides" (cf. Numbers 33:55; Joshua 23:13).
notes.2:18: "Was moved to pity" renders the Niphal imperfect yinnachem (from nacham), which paired with min ("by") denotes being moved to compassion or relenting in response to distress.
notes.2:19: "Did not give up" translates the Hiphil perfect lo hippilu (from naphal, literally "did not let fall" or "drop"), used idiomatically for refusing to abandon entrenched practices.
notes.2:22: Hebrew literally reads "to walk in them" (bam, masculine plural suffix), referring ad sensum to the singular collective "the way of the LORD"; rendered "in it" for English clarity.
notes.3:2: The Hebrew syntax is compact: the Qal infinitive construct da'at ('knowing') is clarified by the Piel infinitive construct lelammedam ('to instruct them'). The masculine plural suffix on yeda'um ('had known them') refers back to the wars of Canaan in verse 1.
notes.3:15: Literally 'a man restricted in his right hand' (itter yad-yemino), an idiom for being left-handed that creates irony with his tribal designation 'Benjaminite' (ben-hayemini, literally 'son of the right-hander').
notes.3:16: Hebrew gomed occurs only here in the Hebrew Bible and refers to a short cubit, roughly the length of a forearm to the knuckles.
notes.3:22: Hebrew happarshedonah occurs only here and its meaning is uncertain; traditionally linked to peresh ('excrement/dung'), though its penultimate stress resembles a directional -ah ending (as in v. 23), which could indicate 'out at the rear' or a part of the chamber.
notes.3:24: Literally 'covering his feet' (mesik et-raglaw), a Hebrew euphemism for relieving oneself (cf. 1 Samuel 24:3).
notes.4:6: The Qal verb mashak ('draw, pull') is used intransitively here in a military sense ('deploy, march out,' cf. Judges 20:37), setting up a wordplay with the transitive use of the same verb in verse 7 ('I will draw out').
notes.4:11: Ketiv reads bts'nym (likely 'in Zaanim'); Qere reads beza'anannim ('in Zaanannim,' cf. Joshua 19:33), which is followed here. 'Kain' (Qayin) is the eponymous clan name of the Kenites.
notes.4:20: Hebrew 'amod ('Stand') is vocalized as a masculine singular imperative addressed to Jael, whereas the following verbs addressing her are feminine singular.
notes.4:21: The feminine singular verb wattisnah ('and it went down') takes the feminine noun hayyated ('the peg') as its subject. Hebrew wayya'ap ('and exhausted') is a Qal wayyiqtol of 'up ('be faint/exhausted,' cf. 1 Samuel 14:28, 31), continuing the circumstantial explanation of Sisera's state.
notes.5:2: Hebrew bipheroa pera'ot (Qal infinitive construct plus cognate plural noun from para') literally means "when locks hang loose," likely referring to consecrated warriors unbinding their hair for battle (cf. Num 6:5; Deut 32:42); alternatively, from an Arabic cognate, "when leaders took the lead."
notes.5:5: The verb nazelu is vocalized in the MT as Qal perfect of nazal ("flowed/streamed"), though some link it to zalal ("quaked"). The archaic phrase zeh Sinai ("the One of Sinai") uses zeh as a relative epithet for God, or alternatively means "even Sinai."
notes.5:11: The hapax Piel participle mehatsetsim is uncertain: traditionally taken as a denominative from hets ("arrow") meaning "archers" (with privative min in miqqol, "away from the sound of"), or alternatively "musicians" or "those who divide" ("to the sound of").
notes.5:13: The unusual MT verb form yerad (occurring twice) is generally taken as a poetic form of yarad ("went down," matching vv. 11 and 14), though traditionally parsed from radah ("had dominion"). The clause break follows the Masoretic athnach after 'am ("the people").
notes.5:30: The MT literally reads letsavvere shalal, "for the necks of the plunder" (likely referring to garments draped around necks as spoil, or to captive spoil); some ancient versions read "for my neck" or "for the necks of the spoilers."
notes.6:5: Ketiv reads the Qal imperfect yavo'u ("they would come"), while the Qere followed here reads the frequentative weqatal uva'u ("and they would come in").
notes.6:15: Whereas Gideon addressed his visitor as 'adoni ("my lord") in 6:13, here the MT vocalizes 'adonai ("Lord"), reflecting his direct address to the LORD who spoke in 6:14.
notes.6:25: The MT literally reads "the young bull of the cattle that belongs to your father, and the second bull, seven years old." The conjunction "and" may refer to a second bull (the one sacrificed in vv. 26 and 28) or function epexegetically ("even the second bull").
notes.6:34: Hebrew laveshah 'et-Gid'on literally means "put on Gideon" or "clothed itself with Gideon" (Qal perfect of lavash), a vivid idiom depicting the Spirit enveloping and empowering him as a person puts on a garment.
notes.7:3: The verb rendered "depart" (Qal jussive of ts-p-r) is a Biblical Hebrew hapax legomenon whose exact nuance is uncertain, possibly "depart early" or "hurry away." The Masoretic Text explicitly reads "Mount Gilead," though Gilead normally refers to the highlands east of the Jordan.
notes.7:5: The Masoretic Hebrew ends the verse elliptically after "to drink," leaving the instruction to set this second group apart as well implied from the preceding clause.
notes.7:8: The phrase "the provisions of the people" follows the definite object marker (et-) before an uninflected feminine noun (tsedah) joined to "the people," with the three hundred men as the plural subject; alternatively, "the people" may be read as the subject ("the people took provisions").
notes.7:15: The noun rendered "interpretation" literally means "breaking" (breaking open the meaning of a dream), and "account" (mispar, usually "number") echoes the Piel verb "recounting" in verse 13.
notes.7:21: Following the Qere (Qal of n-w-s, "and fled"); the Ketiv reflects a Hiphil form ("and put to flight" or "carried off in flight").
notes.8:13: The Masoretic Hebrew reads "by the ascent of Heres," taking ha-cheres (literally "the sun") as a place name; some ancient versions interpret the phrase temporally as "before sunrise."
notes.8:16: The Masoretic Hebrew reads a defective Hiphil form of y-d-' ("to know"), literally "he made [them] know," idiomatically "taught a lesson" (or possibly a homonymous root meaning "subdue/humiliate"); some ancient versions read "threshed" as in verse 7.
notes.8:18: The interrogative ephoh normally means "where?" but uniquely asks here about quality or appearance ("what were they like?"), as confirmed by the kings' comparison.
notes.8:26: Literally "one thousand seven hundred gold"; Biblical Hebrew regularly omits the standard unit of weight ("shekels") before a metal.
notes.9:8: Ketiv reads mlwkh and Qere reads molkhah, a Qal masculine singular imperative of malakh with paragogic -ah, meaning Reign. The same orthographic variant preserving the internal o-vowel occurs in 9:12 with Ketiv mlwky and Qere molkhi, the feminine singular imperative.
notes.9:17: Risked his life renders the Hebrew idiom literally meaning cast his life away, using the Hiphil of shalakh with minneged.
notes.9:29: The Masoretic Text reads the third-person wayyiqtol And he said to Abimelech, framing Gaal's words as a rhetorical taunt or challenge, rather than a first-person conditional statement.
notes.9:31: Secretly translates the rare noun in betormah, literally in craftiness or stealth from the root ramah, though some read it as a place name, Tormah. Fortifying renders the Qal plural participle tsarim from tsur, meaning enclose, fortify, or besiege, which is often taken contextually as stirring up.
notes.9:44: The Masoretic Text has the plural the divisions with Abimelech, even though 9:43 mentions three divisions in total and the second clause names the two divisions.
notes.10:4: The Masoretic Text points both occurrences of the plural noun identically as ayarim, creating a pun between 'donkey colts' (plural of ayir) and 'towns' (normally arim).
notes.10:8: The Hebrew pairs two alliterative verbs from closely related roots, Qal ra'ats ('shatter') and Polel ratsats ('crush/oppress'), intensifying the harshness of the oppression.
notes.10:11: The Masoretic Hebrew lacks an explicit verb in this verse (an anacoluthon), with the implied verb 'deliver' supplied from the climax in verse 12 ('and I delivered you').
notes.10:16: Literally 'His soul grew short over the misery of Israel,' a Hebrew idiom expressing the limit of endurance or patience.
notes.11:13: The Masoretic Text uses a feminine plural pronoun ('them') following singular 'my land,' referring collectively to the cities or tracts within that territory.
notes.11:31: The masculine singular participle ('the one who comes out') and object suffix ('that one') are grammatically generic in Hebrew; the conjunction 'and' literally connects belonging to the LORD with offering as a burnt offering.
notes.11:34: The Masoretic Text literally reads 'from him' (mimmennu), understood either as having no other child 'of his own' or as a rare masculine-for-feminine suffix meaning 'besides her.'
notes.11:37: The qere (read text) is plural 'and my companions' (matching verse 38), whereas the ketiv (written text) appears to reflect a singular form ('and my companion') or an older plural spelling. The verb 'go down' (yarad) literally describes descending onto the mountain slopes and is often understood as wandering over the hills.
notes.11:40: The rare Piel verb tanah ('recount, commemorate,' as in Judges 5:11) is also commonly understood in this context as 'lament.'
notes.12:1: Hebrew tsaphonah may be understood either as the town 'to Zaphon' in the Jordan valley (cf. Josh 13:27) or directionally as 'northward.'
notes.12:2: The clause rendered 'were in a severe dispute' is literally 'a man of strife I was, I and my people and the sons of Ammon, greatly' (ish riv).
notes.12:4: The Ephraimites' taunt is terse in Hebrew and sets up the verbal irony of 'the fugitives of Ephraim' (pelite Ephrayim) in v. 5.
notes.12:6: The verb yakhin is a Hiphil imperfect of kun ('establish, direct'), used idiomatically for managing to pronounce the word properly; Hebrew contrasts the sibilants sh in shibbolet and s in sibbolet.
notes.13:8: The form hayyullad ('who is to be born') is a Pual participle of yalad without the usual mem prefix, expressing imminent or destined birth.
notes.13:12: Hebrew pairs a singular verb (yavo) with a plural subject (devarekha, 'your words'); mishpat ('rule') and ma'asehu ('his work') refer to the boy's prescribed regimen and calling.
notes.13:17: Ketiv reads plural 'your words' (matching v. 12), while Qere (translated here) reads singular devarkha ('your word') in strict agreement with the singular verb yavo.
notes.13:19: The Hiphil participle umaphli ('doing a wondrous thing,' echoing the adjective peli'i, 'wonderful,' in v. 18) has no explicit subject in Hebrew; following the Masoretic punctuation, it describes the angel of the LORD acting wondrously (detailed in v. 20), though some take the LORD as its subject.
notes.13:25: The infinitive lepha'amo ('to stir him') is the sole Qal occurrence of pa'am in Biblical Hebrew, denoting a strong impelling impulse; Mahaneh-dan means 'Camp of Dan.'
notes.14:4: The noun to'anah ('pretext' or 'occasion' for confrontation) occurs only here in Biblical Hebrew, and the pronoun 'He' refers back to the LORD.
notes.14:9: The verb radah ('scraped out') is a homonym distinct from the verb 'to rule' and appears only in this verse in Biblical Hebrew.
notes.14:15: The Masoretic Hebrew reads 'on the seventh day' (unlike the Septuagint and Syriac, which read 'on the fourth day'); the final interrogative particle halo ('Is it not so?') is likewise translated as preserved in the Masoretic text.
notes.14:18: Hebrew hacharsah ('the sun') uses the rare poetic noun cheres ('sun') with a poetic or archaic -ah ending.
notes.14:20: The verb re'ah ('acted as his friend') is a rare Piel form cognate with mere'ehu ('his companion'), denoting the groom's special attendant or best man.
notes.15:8: The phrase "leg upon thigh" renders the Hebrew idiom shoq al-yarekh, expressing a thorough, crushing defeat.
notes.15:16: Samson's saying puns on the Hebrew homonym chamor, meaning both "donkey" and "heap," paired with the dual chamoratayim ("two heaps").
notes.15:19: Hebrew maktesh denotes a mortar-shaped hollow or basin, and the spring name En-hakkore means "Spring of the One Who Calls," echoing Samson's calling out in v. 18; "in Lehi" (ba-lechi) also plays on "in the jawbone."
notes.16:2: The Masoretic Text is elliptical at the opening of the verse, reading literally "To the Gazites, saying," with the introductory verb "it was reported" implied.
notes.16:13: The Masoretic Text omits Samson's expected consequence at the end of v. 13 and Delilah's act of weaving at the start of v. 14, leaving both implicit from the preceding episodes.
notes.16:18: Ketiv reads "to her" (indirect speech within the messenger's report), whereas Qere reads "to me" (direct speech), followed here.
notes.16:21: Qere reads "the house of those bound" (Qal passive participle asurim, echoed in v. 25), whereas Ketiv reads the noun form "the house of the prisoners" (asirim).
notes.16:25: Qere reads ke-tov (preposition plus Qal infinitive construct, "when [their hearts] were merry"), while Ketiv reads ki tov (conjunction plus Qal perfect); the same ketiv/qere on "prison house" recurs from v. 21.
notes.16:26: Qere reads the Hiphil imperative of mush ("let me feel"), whereas Ketiv reflects a by-form from the root ymsh with the same meaning.
notes.16:28: Hebrew neqam-achat mi-shetei einai ("vengeance for one of my two eyes," with feminine achat matching feminine ayin, "eye") can alternatively be construed adverbially as "vengeance at one stroke for my two eyes."
notes.17:1: Verses 1 and 4 spell the name in its fuller Masoretic form Mikayehu ("Who is like the LORD?"), while vv. 5-13 use the shortened form Mikah ("Micah").
notes.17:2: Qere reads the standard second-person feminine singular pronoun at ("you"), whereas Ketiv preserves the archaic spelling atti.
notes.17:4: The paired terms "a carved image and a cast image" (pesel u-massekhah) take a singular verb ("it was"), pointing either to a single composite metal-plated wooden idol or to grammatical agreement with the collective "silver."
notes.17:5: Hebrew beit elohim ("a house of gods," or "a house of God") denotes a private shrine, and "installed" translates the priestly ordination idiom mille et-yad, literally "filled the hand of" (also in v. 12).
notes.18:7: The difficult Masoretic phrase rendered "no possessor of authority in the land humiliating anyone in any matter" literally reads "none putting to shame (Hiphil participle of kalam) in any matter in the land, a possessor of restraint (yoresh etser)," referring to the absence of any governing ruler to check or harass them.
notes.18:18: The Masoretic Text reads the construct phrase "the carved image of the ephod" (lacking both the definite article on "carved image" and the conjunction found in 18:17); some treat it asyndetically as "the carved image, the ephod."
notes.18:25: Literally "and you will gather in your life and the life of your household" (Qal of asaph), an idiom meaning to bring about one's own death and that of one's household.
notes.18:30: The Masoretic Text reads "Manasseh," traditionally written with a suspended letter nun; omitting that letter yields "Moses," reflecting an ancient scribal tradition linking Jonathan son of Gershom to Moses (cf. Exod 2:22).
notes.19:2: The Masoretic verb (Qal of zanah with al) literally means "committed sexual unfaithfulness against him"; some ancient versions render instead "became angry with him."
notes.19:3: Translating the Qere (read form), "to bring her back" (Hiphil infinitive construct of shuv with 3fs suffix); the Ketiv (written form) has a masculine suffix ("to bring him/it back").
notes.19:18: The Masoretic Text reads "to the house of the LORD" (using et idiomatically to mark destination with halakh); the Septuagint reads "to my house."
notes.19:21: Translating the Qere, "and gave fodder" (Qal wayyiqtol of balal, meaning to mix or provide provender); the Ketiv preserves a plene spelling of the same verb form.
notes.19:25: Translating the Qere, "as the dawn was rising" (preposition ke- with Qal infinitive construct of alah); the Ketiv reads the preposition be- ("at the rising of the dawn").
notes.20:13: The words "sons of" (Hebrew bene) reflect a Masoretic qere reading that is read in tradition though absent from the consonantal text, which writes only "Benjamin" with a plural verb.
notes.20:33: Hebrew maareh is a hapax legomenon from the root meaning "be bare" or "exposed," denoting open or bare ground (or possibly a place name, Maareh-geba). Here and in 20:10 the Masoretic Text reads "Geba" rather than "Gibeah."
notes.20:38: The form herev is a shortened Hiphil imperative or infinitive of ravah ("make great"), used adverbially before the Hiphil infinitive construct "their causing to rise" to describe sending up a great signal plume (masat) of smoke.
notes.20:43: The Hebrew phrase menuhah hidrikuhu is difficult: menuhah literally means "resting place" (perhaps a place name, Menuhah, or adverbially "with ease"), and hidrikuhu is a Hiphil of darakh meaning "trod down" or "overtook."
notes.20:48: Literally "from a city of completeness" (Hebrew meir metom, from the root tamam, "be complete"), denoting the entire city and its population; compare the similar phrase "city of inhabitants" (ir metim) in Deuteronomy 2:34.
notes.21:14: Hebrew literally reads "and they did not find for them thus"; the Qal of matsa with the preposition le- idiomatically expresses sufficiency, indicating that the four hundred women were still not enough for the surviving Benjaminites.
notes.21:17: Hebrew uses a terse verbless clause, literally "an inheritance of an escaped remnant for Benjamin," conveying that the surviving Benjaminites must have descendants to preserve their tribal inheritance.
notes.21:20: Qere reads the Piel plural wayyetsawwu ("and they commanded"), matching the plural elders of vv. 16-19; ketiv writes the Piel singular wayyetsaw ("and he commanded"), likely agreeing with the congregation as a collective.
notes.21:22: Qere reads the Qal infinitive construct lariv ("to contend") where ketiv writes the medial-waw by-form larov. The closing clause is elliptical in Hebrew (literally "for you did not give to them, at this time you would be guilty"), arguing that because the fathers did not give their daughters voluntarily, they avoid incurring the guilt of breaking the oath.
